item.title: Aeromexico says fresh US routes to be unveiled next week
item.description: Aeromexico will likely unveil a first batch of new US routes as soon as next week, Chief Executive Andres Conesa said on Tuesday, offering the clearest sign yet that Mexico's flagship carrier is moving quickly to capitalize on Washington's decision to lift restrictions on flights from Mexico City.
item.dc:creator: Kylie Madry
item.content:encoded: Aeromexico (AERO.MX) will likely unveil a first batch of new US routes as soon as next week, Chief Executive Andres Conesa said on Tuesday, offering the clearest sign yet that Mexico's flagship carrier is moving quickly to capitalize on Washington's decision to [USN:S0N44F01O TEXT:"lift restrictions"] on flights from Mexico City. Speaking to journalists on the sidelines of the Latin American & Caribbean Air Transport Association conference in Mexico City, Conesa said Aeromexico was weighing several US destinations but was holding off on naming them until it secures permits and airport slots. He said a first package of routes could launch early next year, with another potentially around mid-2027 Last week, the US Department of Transportation scrapped curbs that had blocked Mexican airlines from adding new service from Mexico City's Benito Juarez airport and Felipe Angeles airport Conesa pointed to San Juan, Puerto Rico as one route likely to return, though he said that service was more likely in the second half of 2027 due to the cruise season The executive also said Aeromexico now expects to resume flights to Caracas in the first quarter of 2027, later than previously planned [USN:L1N46503M TEXT:"Flight plans"] to the Venezuelan capital have been snarled by the deadly twin earthquakes earlier this year Aeromexico is pressing ahead with expansion even as [USN:L1N4660X4 TEXT:"fuel costs bite"], though Conesa said airlines had been forced to raise fares to reflect the surge in jet fuel prices

item.title: PSG sink Barcelona in six-goal thriller, Liverpool and Man City win
item.description: Paris St Germain underlined their status as European champions by beating Barcelona 4-2 in a blockbuster Champions League clash on Tuesday, while Liverpool and Manchester City also claimed victories.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Paris St Germain underlined their status as European champions by beating Barcelona 4-2 in a blockbuster Champions League clash on Tuesday, while Liverpool and Manchester City also claimed victories. Desire Doue, Lucas Hernandez, Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz scored for PSG, with Xavi Espart and Lamine Yamal twice pulling Barcelona level in the second half. Alexis Mac Allister scored twice as Liverpool fought back from two goals down to beat Villarreal 4-3 in a thrilling encounter at Anfield. Phil Foden scored a hat-trick to lead Manchester City to a 5-1 win over AEK Athens at the Etihad Stadium, with Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki also on the scoresheet as Erling Haaland was rested. PSG OUTLAST BARCELONA Barcelona arrived at the Parc des Princes with a perfect record across all competitions this season, but PSG proved more clinical in a breathless contest to hand the Catalans their first defeat of the campaign. The relentless tempo took its toll, with PSG's Ousmane Dembele, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Marquinhos, along with Barcelona's Dani Olmo, all forced off through injury. PSG peppered the Barcelona goal in the opening five minutes, with Kvaratskhelia hitting the post, before the game settled into a rhythm. The hosts gradually took control of midfield and went ahead after Yamal surrendered possession in his own half, allowing Doue to drive a fierce low shot into the corner. Goalkeeper Joan Garcia produced several saves to keep Barcelona in the contest before Espart, making his first Champions League start, created and finished a superb move to equalise in the 55th minute. Ferran Torres hit the post against his former club before Hernandez headed PSG in front from a corner in the 72nd minute, starting a burst of four goals in 14 minutes. Lamine equalised again for Barcelona with a brilliant individual effort in the 79th minute, before Vitinha responded for PSG with a fine strike 109 seconds later. As Hansi Flick's side searched for an equaliser, Fabian Ruiz converted an Achraf Hakimi cross at the back post to seal the victory. The result lifted PSG onto nine points and top of the Champions League standings, ahead of Liverpool on goal difference. FODEN HITS THREE Foden netted a hat-trick as Man City comfortably dispatched AEK Athens at the Etihad Stadium. Anderson opened the scoring for the hosts in the 12th minute before Foden doubled the advantage in the 34th. AEK Athens pulled a goal back through Stavros Pilios in the 52nd minute, but Cherki restored City's two-goal cushion five minutes later. Foden added his second of the night in the 65th minute and completed his treble 11 minutes later to wrap up a dominant performance. Haaland was an unused substitute, as City gave their leading striker a rest amid a demanding fixture schedule. Liverpool edged Spanish side Villarreal after a stirring comeback. The visitors stunned the home crowd when Georges Mikautadze struck in the fourth minute before Sergi Cardona doubled Villarreal's lead in the 29th. Liverpool's fightback started with two headers as Mac Allister pulled a goal back in the 36th minute before Ronald Araujo equalised in first-half stoppage time. Mac Allister completed the turnaround with his second goal in the 65th minute, and Florian Wirtz hammered home a fourth in the 69th to cap a rampant spell for the hosts. Tani Oluwaseyi pulled one back for Villarreal in the 87th minute, but Liverpool survived the late pressure to secure the points. Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez levelled in the second half to earn them a 1-1 draw with VfB Stuttgart, who took the lead through Jamie Leweling before the break. Morten Hjulmand was sent off in the 64th minute, leaving Atletico with 10 men for the closing stages. Napoli edged Bodo/Glimt 4-3 and PSV Eindhoven held off Porto for a 1-0 win, while AS Roma cruised to a 4-0 victory over Slovan Bratislava. Earlier, Borussia Dortmund won 2-1 against Champions League debutants Sabah, while a 90th-minute equaliser from Pavel Kacor earned Slavia Prague a point in a 2-2 draw at Fenerbahce.

item.title: Aerolíneas Argentinas no solicitará fondos estatales pese a presión por precio de combustible: CEO
item.description: Aerolíneas Argentinas descartó solicitar más financiación gubernamental pese al alza del precio del combustible, dijo su director ejecutivo a Reuters, después de que registrara resultados positivos en 2024 y 2025, y en un momento en que el presidente Javier Milei impulsa la privatización de la empresa.
item.dc:creator: Kylie Madry
item.content:encoded: Aerolíneas Argentinas descartó solicitar más financiación gubernamental pese al alza del precio del combustible, dijo su director ejecutivo a Reuters, después de que registrara resultados positivos en 2024 y 2025, y en un momento en que el presidente Javier Milei impulsa la privatización de la empresa. Fabián Lombardo afirmó el martes que la aerolínea se había convertido en una empresa financieramente autosuficiente tras reducir la plantilla, optimizar los procesos y mejorar la eficiencia, siguiendo el mandato del Gobierno de Milei de mantenerla en funcionamiento sin que supusiera un coste para el Estado. "La compañía tenía que seguir volando, pero sin perder dinero para el Estado", dijo Lombardo, hablando al margen de una conferencia de la Asociación Latinoamericana y Caribeña de Transporte Aéreo. Lombardo afirmó que la última transferencia gubernamental a la empresa se realizó en 2024 y no prevé solicitar más dinero al Estado, a pesar de que los precios del combustible están afectando a los resultados. "El costo que se aumenta definitivamente es por combustible", dijo Lombardo, y agregó que los demás costos se habían mantenido bajo control. Estas declaraciones marcan un giro radical para Aerolíneas Argentinas [RIC:RIC:AERA.UL], al que el Gobierno ha descrito durante mucho tiempo como un símbolo de la ineficiencia estatal. El Gobierno de Milei anunció que procedería a privatizarla por decreto, declarándola sujeta a privatización tras afirmar que la aerolínea había recibido más de 8.000 millones de dólares en ayudas estatales desde su renacionalización en 2008. Lombardo afirmó que el objetivo del Gobierno seguía siendo la privatización, pero que el papel de la dirección es dejar la empresa en condiciones lo suficientemente buenas como para que los políticos decidieran su futuro. El Congreso, añadió, tendría que desempeñar un papel en cualquier proceso de venta. Lombardo también señaló que Aerolíneas se había beneficiado de la inestabilidad en otros sectores del mercado de la aviación nacional argentina. Explicó que los problemas de su rival de bajo costo Flybondi, que suspendió sus vuelos en agosto, habían obligado a la competencia a absorber casi 300.000 asientos. "Nosotros tomamos una posición rápida de captar ese mercado", dijo, y agregó que Aerolíneas ahora controla alrededor del 70% del mercado interno. El sector de la aviación argentina se ha transformado gracias a la desregulación impulsada por el Gobierno de Milei. En 2024, el Gobierno implementó una reforma integral de "cielos abiertos" para facilitar la entrada de aerolíneas extranjeras a un mercado dominado durante mucho tiempo por Aerolíneas. Este mes, Argentina autorizó a la chilena JetSMART a operar servicios de pasajeros y carga, tanto nacionales como internacionales, en el país. Lombardo afirmó que Aerolíneas no estaba preocupada por la medida, y describió la competencia adicional como marginal.

item.title: Musk ordered slowdown of Starlink service used by Ukraine's military, WSJ reports
item.description: Elon Musk last week ordered the slowdown of a military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink satellite service that Ukraine relies on, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday, citing US officials and people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Elon Musk last week ordered the slowdown of a military-grade version of SpaceX's (SPCX.O) Starlink satellite service that Ukraine relies on, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday, citing US officials and people familiar with the matter. Musk, SpaceX and the White House did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Ukraine uses Starlink for battlefield communications and drone operations. Restricting the satellite service [USN:L8N4600M6 TEXT:"hampered"] the country's attack and air defense drone missions against Russia. Musk and US President Donald Trump discussed the Starlink decision in a call soon after the slowdown became public, while the president was campaigning last week, according to the report, which added the two had also discussed the matter prior to the decision to throttle Starlink. Reuters had [USN:L1N4610ZC TEXT:"reported"] exclusively that the order to limit the satellite system came from inside the White House. Trump said last week he did not think either he or Musk was responsible for Ukraine losing Starlink access, while Musk said any limits on speed or Starship use were decided by the US military or the president. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy's relations with Washington have sunk to new lows after Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel and waived new sanctions on Moscow. Trump has also told Kyiv to stop attacking Russian refineries and urged Ukrainians to replace Zelenskiy. Zelenskiy, who is in Oslo in a bid to repair US relations, said on Tuesday he [USN:L8N46606A TEXT:"discussed"] issues including "the situation with Starlink/Starshield, which needs to be restored" with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth [USN:SPN4650B4 TEXT:"said"] on Tuesday Washington had not pulled back Ukraine's ability to access Starling's satellite network, but signaled the problem lay with the terms of service Kyiv needed to comply with.

item.title: California law school wins fight over 'Hastings' namesake as US Supreme Court denies challenge
item.description: The University of California College of the Law, San Francisco is here to stay after nearly a decade of wrangling over its founder's legacy.
item.dc:creator: Karen Sloan
item.content:encoded: The University of California College of the Law, San Francisco is here to stay after nearly a decade of wrangling over its founder's legacy. The US Supreme Court on Monday declined to take up a challenge by descendants of the law school’s former namesake, Serranus Hastings, seeking to block the school’s 2023 [USN:L1N2Z9245 TEXT:"name change"]. The justices' denial caps nine years of debate and litigation over the school’s original moniker — the University of California Hastings College of the Law — named for Hastings, a former California Supreme Court judge who historians say also orchestrated the deaths of Native Americans on land he owned. UC San Francisco Law Dean David Faigman said Tuesday that the school is “pleased to see this chapter behind us” and that the decision to rename the school followed a “robust process.” Attorney Gregory Michael, who represented the Hastings descendants and law school alumni who sued to reverse the name change, said the plaintiffs are disappointed that the Supreme Court turned away their case. “This litigation sought to vindicate fundamental constitutional principles and preserve the legacy of Judge Hastings against legislative action we believe exceeded constitutional limits,” he said. Hastings founded the law school in 1878 with a $100,000 donation. The school announced in 2022 that it would drop the Hastings name following an extensive review of Serranus Hastings' legacy, which was launched after historians said he orchestrated killings of Native Americans in order to remove them from ranch land he purchased in Northern California. A group of law school alumni and six Hastings descendants [USN:L1N3152K8 TEXT:"sued"] the state and school officials in October 2022, claiming the name change breached the 1878 agreement California made with Hastings when he gave money to start a law school that bore his name. A San Francisco judge [USN:L1N3ES2Q8 TEXT:"dismissed"] the suit in 2024, finding that the 1878 legislation that established the law school was not a contract and the 2022 legislation that codified the new name did not violate the California Constitution. A California appellate court affirmed that dismissal in 2025 and the California Supreme Court in January declined to hear the case. Read more: [USN:L1N2Z9245 TEXT:"UC Hastings is history as law school drops controversial namesake"] [USN:L1N3152K8 TEXT:"UC Hastings law school sued by namesake's heirs over name change"]

item.title: -Três temas que marcam as eleições de meio de mandato de 2026 nos EUA
item.description: A popularidade do presidente Donald Trump, que atingiu um nível historicamente baixo, a frustração dos eleitores com o custo de vida e uma acirrada disputa sobre a imigração estão moldando as eleições de meio de mandato de 3 de novembro, que determinarão se os republicanos manterão o controle do Congresso ou se os democratas conquistarão o poder para desafiar seu governo.
item.dc:creator: Nolan Mccaskill
item.content:encoded: A popularidade do presidente Donald Trump, que atingiu um nível historicamente baixo, a frustração dos eleitores com o custo de vida e uma acirrada disputa sobre a imigração estão moldando as eleições de meio de mandato de 3 de novembro, que determinarão se os republicanos manterão o controle do Congresso ou se os democratas conquistarão o poder para desafiar seu governo. Os republicanos detêm maiorias estreitas na Câmara dos Deputados e no Senado. Os democratas precisam de um ganho líquido de quatro cadeiras para assumir o controle de cada uma das Casas. O resultado dependerá de um número relativamente pequeno de disputas acirradas, mas as campanhas estão sendo moldadas em nível nacional pelo próprio Trump e pelas preocupações dos eleitores com o custo de vida e a imigração. Veja a seguir os três temas que definem a eleição: DONALD TRUMP O presidente colocou-se no centro das atenções na reta final do ciclo eleitoral, apesar de sua popularidade estar em nível recorde de baixa, com comícios programados na Flórida, em Iowa, em Michigan e no Texas. O índice de aprovação de Trump caiu para 31%, o menor nível já registrado, de acordo com uma pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos. No entanto, ele tem repetidamente instado os eleitores a fingirem que ele está na cédula eleitoral — uma estratégia que poderia motivar democratas e independentes a se unirem contra seu partido, embora a mensagem tenha como objetivo aumentar a participação eleitoral entre a base de Trump. Os democratas afirmam que Trump não cumpriu suas promessas de campanha de reduzir custos e pôr fim às guerras. Eles prometeram adotar uma agenda de acessibilidade para reduzir o custo de vida dos norte-americanos e responsabilizar o governo por supostas práticas de corrupção, caso os eleitores lhes concedam o controle de qualquer uma das duas Casas do Congresso. CUSTO DE VIDA Os eleitores têm consistentemente classificado o custo de vida como o principal tema neste ciclo eleitoral. Metade dos eleitores registrados entrevistados em uma pesquisa recente Reuters/Ipsos citou o custo de vida como o fator mais importante na decisão de voto. Na mesma pesquisa, os eleitores destacaram saúde, gasolina, alimentação e moradia como as principais despesas domésticas nas quais os parlamentares deveriam se concentrar. A principal conquista legislativa dos republicanos foi a prorrogação de um corte de impostos que reduziu em cerca de US$1 trilhão os gastos com o Medicaid — o programa governamental de seguro saúde para norte-americanos de baixa renda — e outros programas de saúde. No ano passado, os democratas forçaram uma paralisação do governo devido a uma tentativa fracassada de prorrogar subsídios de saúde que estavam prestes a expirar e que beneficiavam 24 milhões de norte-americanos. Os preços da gasolina dispararam desde que os EUA e Israel lançaram ataques militares contra o Irã em fevereiro. O preço médio nacional da gasolina é de US$4,28 — US$1,20 a mais do que há um ano, segundo a AAA. O custo médio do diesel é de US$6,32 — um aumento de US$2,70 em relação ao ano anterior. Os custos com mantimentos subiram 1,8% no último ano, de acordo com dados do Departamento de Estatísticas do Trabalho dos EUA sobre preços ao consumidor. Dados da Agência Federal de Financiamento Imobiliário mostram que os preços das casas subiram 2,1% no último ano. O Congresso aprovou um projeto de lei bipartidário sobre habitação no início deste ano. Ele se tornou lei sem a assinatura de Trump. IMIGRAÇÃO Dados preliminares do Departamento de Segurança Interna mostraram uma queda de 95% no número de migrantes detidos na fronteira sudoeste em comparação com o governo do ex-presidente Joe Biden. A agência informou que, pela primeira vez na história, não houve nenhuma liberação pela Patrulha de Fronteira durante todo o ano fiscal. No entanto, ocorreram confrontos fatais com agentes federais de imigração no Maine, em Minnesota e no Texas. A reação à morte de dois cidadãos norte-americanos em Minnesota levou muitos democratas em primárias acirradas a se posicionarem mais à esquerda este ano, com alguns candidatos pedindo o impeachment da então secretária de Segurança Interna, Kristi Noem, e outros defendendo que o Serviço de Imigração e Alfândega (ICE) deveria ser abolido. Democratas e republicanos entraram em choque sobre o financiamento da imigração este ano, o que forçou os republicanos a aprovar unilateralmente um projeto de lei de US$70 bilhões para financiar o ICE e a Patrulha de Fronteira até o fim do mandato de Trump. Os republicanos rebatem as críticas dos democratas alegando que estes defendem fronteiras abertas. Autoridades federais de imigração também realizaram uma operação na residência em Washington da deputada federal democrata Ilhan Omar, de Minnesota, neste mês, o que gerou ampla condenação por parte dos democratas. Uma pessoa a par do processo contra Omar disse à Reuters que um dos possíveis objetivos da investigação poderia ser retirar-lhe a cidadania norte-americana e deportá-la. OUTROS TEMAS Inteligência artificial e data centers, criptomoedas, aborto e Israel também podem influenciar os eleitores em disputas eleitorais específicas. Na disputa pelo Senado em Ohio, por exemplo, o candidato democrata Sherrod Brown rotulou o senador republicano Jon Husted como o rosto dos data centers, e o super PAC de criptomoedas “Defend American Jobs” gastou mais de US$46 milhões para reeleger Husted em detrimento de Brown, um ex-senador que presidiu a Comissão de Bancos da Câmara. Na disputa pelo Senado no Maine, o candidato democrata Troy Jackson espera que os eleitores não se esqueçam de que a senadora republicana Susan Collins ajudou a confirmar Brett Kavanaugh para a Suprema Corte, que posteriormente revogou o direito federal ao aborto. Collins está na cédula eleitoral pela primeira vez desde que a Suprema Corte transformou o aborto em uma questão estadual, em vez de um direito federal. Em Michigan, o candidato republicano Mike Rogers indicou que aceitaria ajuda de um super PAC pró-Israel que gastou mais de US$30 milhões apoiando a deputada democrata Haley Stevens em sua primária malsucedida contra Abdul El-Sayed, que agora enfrenta Rogers na eleição geral. O grupo já gastou mais de US$280 mil em correspondências contra El-Sayed. No início desta semana, Trump declarou seu apoio à reeleição do primeiro-ministro israelense, Benjamin Netanyahu.

item.title: Soja e milho caem para novas mínimas em várias semanas em Chicago
item.description: Os contratos futuros da soja negociados em Chicago caíram para uma nova mínima de dois meses nesta terça-feira, enquanto o milho atingiu a menor cotação em dois meses e meio, devido à liquidação de posições compradas por fundos e à pressão causada pela colheita em andamento, que deve resultar em safras recordes nos EUA.
item.dc:creator: Karl Plume
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros da soja negociados em Chicago caíram para uma nova mínima de dois meses nesta terça-feira, enquanto o milho atingiu a menor cotação em dois meses e meio, devido à liquidação de posições compradas por fundos e à pressão causada pela colheita em andamento, que deve resultar em safras recordes nos EUA. Os futuros do trigo seguiram o mesmo caminho do milho e da soja na bolsa, caindo para o nível mais baixo desde meados de julho devido a vendas técnicas e por parte dos fundos, além da queda na demanda. As previsões de que o clima favorável à colheita no Meio-Oeste se mantenha pelo menos até o final desta semana pressionaram os mercados de grãos, à medida que os agricultores colhiam uma safra recorde de soja e o que se projeta ser a segunda maior safra de milho já registrada. A pressão da colheita ofuscou a renovada demanda chinesa por soja dos EUA, à medida que o Departamento de Agricultura dos EUA confirmou mais compras por parte do maior importador mundial. "Os chineses têm comprado, mas o problema é que estão comprando as 25 milhões (de toneladas métricas) que já sabíamos que iriam comprar. Parece que isso já está incorporado ao cenário", disse Jim McCormick, diretor de operações da AgMarket. "Neste momento, estamos vendo apenas a pressão tradicional de hedge sendo ampliada por alguma liquidação de fundos." Os contratos futuros de soja novembro caíram 5,25 centavos, para US$12,4825 o bushel, o menor valor desde 26 de agosto. Os contratos futuros de milho dezembro recuaram 5 centavos, para US$4,62 o bushel, o menor valor do contrato desde 12 de agosto. O contrato de trigo dezembro recuou 12 centavos, para US$6,4325 o bushel, seu menor valor desde 10 de julho.

item.title: Café arábica cai após atingir a maior cotação em 6 semanas; açúcar fica quase estável

item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros de café arábica da bolsa ICE caíram nesta terça-feira, após atingirem a maior cotação em seis semanas, à medida que as operações de hedge dos produtores e a realização de lucros por parte dos especuladores tiraram a força do mercado. CAFÉ * Os futuros de café arábica fecharam em queda de 4,4 centavos, ou 1,4%, a US$3,113 por libra-peso, após terem atingido, mais cedo, o preço mais alto desde 9 de setembro, de US$3,1820. "Os futuros do arábica deram uma pausa na alta, e as negociações foram mistas ao longo do pregão. As vendas dos produtores e a realização de lucros ocorreram na faixa de 310–315", disse o corretor da StoneX, Tomás Araújo. Os participantes do mercado estão atentos às novas chegadas de lotes de café arábica aos armazéns da ICE, em busca de possíveis aumentos nos estoques certificados. Houve um pequeno aumento nos lotes pendentes de recomendação, mas nada significativo. Uma pesquisa da Cepea/Esalq indicou que o café brasileiro já está formando frutos em algumas áreas, antes do previsto, o que é um sinal de desenvolvimento desigual da safra. O café robusta fechou em queda de US$56, ou 1,6%, a US$3.424 por tonelada métrica. AÇÚCAR • O açúcar bruto fechou em queda de 0,05 centavo, ou 0,2%, a 20,52 centavos por libra-peso. * Os corretores afirmaram que o mercado parece estar em fase de consolidação, após atingir na semana passada uma máxima de 19 meses, de 21,29. Os fundos mantêm uma posição comprada recorde, por isso consideram que o mercado está sujeito a uma correção. * O analista Michael McDougall afirmou que as usinas brasileiras provavelmente deixaram de produzir mais 1 milhão de toneladas na produção de açúcar na primeira quinzena de outubro devido às chuvas, elevando a perda de produção na safra para 5,7 milhões de toneladas. * O déficit de oferta no mercado global de açúcar, ou seja, a diferença entre produção e demanda, foi projetado na terça-feira para crescer para 6,28 milhões de toneladas, 3 milhões de toneladas a mais do que a estimativa anterior, de acordo com a Green Pool Commodities, empresa de análise de mercado. * O preço do açúcar branco ficou praticamente inalterado em US$547,10 por tonelada. CACAU O cacau de Londres fechou com alta de 65 libras, ou 1,5%, a 4.445 libras por tonelada. "Os preços continuam em uma tendência lateral... a moagem melhor do que o esperado na semana passada não foi um catalisador para uma ruptura", afirmou a corretora StoneX em uma nota. O tempo seco na maior parte do cinturão de cacau da Costa do Marfim na semana passada gerou preocupações sobre possíveis danos às vagens para a safra do próximo ano, segundo os agricultores. O contrato de futuros de cacau de Nova York subiu 2%, para US$5.801 por tonelada. (Reportagem de Gus Trompiz e Marcelo Teixeira)

item.title: Netflix emite débil previsión para el cuarto trimestre, intenta reactivar su crecimiento
item.description: Netflix publicó el martes unas previsiones de beneficios para el cuarto trimestre inferiores a lo esperado, pocos días después de que la empresa pionera en streaming despidiera al 6% de su plantilla y sustituyera a dos de sus principales ejecutivos de programación.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Richwine
item.content:encoded: Netflix (NFLX.O) publicó el martes unas previsiones de beneficios para el cuarto trimestre inferiores a lo esperado, pocos días después de que la empresa pionera en streaming despidiera al 6% de su plantilla y sustituyera a dos de sus principales ejecutivos de programación. Las acciones de Netflix caían casi un 7%, a 63,99 dólares, en las operaciones posteriores al cierre regular del mercado. Los papeles ya se habían hundido más del 40% en términos interanuales antes de la publicación de los resultados. Los ingresos del tercer trimestre aumentaron un 11,8%, a 12.870 millones de dólares, en línea con las previsiones de Wall Street, pero con la tasa de crecimiento más baja en casi tres años. La empresa prevé beneficios netos para el cuarto trimestre de 2.790 millones de dólares y una utilidad por acción de 67 centavos, por debajo de la estimación promedio de los analistas, que se situaba en 3.070 millones de dólares y 73 centavos, respectivamente. Netflix redujo su previsión de ingresos publicitarios para 2026 a casi 2.700 millones de dólares, frente a los aproximadamente 3.000 millones de dólares previstos inicialmente. Algunas funcionalidades de los productos publicitarios se han implementado un poco más lento de lo esperado, indicaron los directivos en su carta trimestral a los accionistas. La compañía que revolucionó Hollywood cuando comenzó a ofrecer series y películas en streaming hace dos décadas se enfrenta ahora a un aumento de la audiencia en YouTube y TikTok. Netflix ha invertido en videojuegos, podcasts y eventos en directo para atraer a nuevos espectadores y aumentar el tiempo que los suscriptores pasan en la plataforma. Los analistas de Wall Street se han preguntado cómo la firma va a reactivar su crecimiento. De cara al futuro, Netflix dijo que seguirá ampliando su oferta mediante la adquisición de licencias de más contenidos de terceros. Más allá de eso, se centrará en su servicio principal de streaming de series, películas y eventos en directo, e invertirá en programas originales que "atraigan a más suscriptores y nos conviertan en un servicio 'imprescindible'", señalaron los directivos en la carta. En el tercer trimestre, el beneficio por acción se situó en 87 centavos, por sobre la previsión promedio de 82 centavos de los analistas encuestados por LSEG. Entre las novedades de programación del trimestre se incluyen "Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story", la segunda temporada de "The Gentlemen", la última entrega de "Outer Banks" y un relanzamiento de "La casa de la pradera". La semana pasada, Netflix despidió a 1.000 personas, lo que supone alrededor del 6% de su plantilla. La empresa sustituyó a la directora creativa, Bela Bajaria, y anunció que el responsable de cine, Dan Lin, abandonaba la empresa, lo que apunta a un replanteamiento de su estrategia de programación. Este año, Netflix perdió la guerra de ofertas por Warner Bros Discovery y su amplia biblioteca de personajes, que fue vendida a Skydance, dirigida por David Ellison . Netflix ha registrado pérdidas mensuales de suscriptores en Estados Unidos durante 2026, sin que se hayan registrado adiciones netas en ningún mes hasta septiembre, según datos de la empresa de análisis Antenna. Antenna realiza un seguimiento de las suscripciones contratadas en Estados Unidos a través de fuentes como las transacciones con tarjeta de crédito, pero excluye las suscripciones adquiridas mediante paquetes al por mayor. Un portavoz de Netflix dijo que los datos de Antenna "no son representativos del desempeño comercial de Netflix".

item.title: SpaceX is stuck in a difficult adolescence
item.description: The $2 trln company’s server-rental unit grew 800%, but attractive returns will probably fade as chip shortages subside. Rockets are boss Elon Musk’s durable advantage, but mostly as a way to support the next big thing. AI, wireless networks, chipmaking or even cars beckon.
item.dc:creator: Robert Cyran
item.content:encoded: What will SpaceX (SPCX.O) be when it grows up? The limitless possibility of a long-prolonged corporate adolescence supported the rocket, satellite network and artificial intelligence company’s ascent to a $2 trillion valuation. Results released on Tuesday highlight the quick returns boss Elon Musk has gleaned from opportunistically expanding into new areas like renting out chips for chatbots. Yet that business could soon erode, leaving the impulsive CEO to search out yet another focus from the many available. SpaceX said that its AI and server-rental unit – renamed to “Super Intelligence,” following President Donald Trump’s preferred terminology – generated an astonishing $7.6 billion of revenue in the third quarter, an 829% increase from last year. This surprise success was the product of arrested development: Musk wanted to run a top AI lab, yet his Grok bot’s also-ran status left its data centers underused. More-popular rivals like Anthropic conversely face a shortage, and paid top dollar to get chips now. This happy accident is now SpaceX’s biggest business line, overtaking its original core focus of putting satellites into orbit with reusable rockets. Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnsen boasted in September that incremental investment in Super Intelligence pays back [USN:L6N45T0Y8 TEXT:"rapidly"], and so the company has said that it could increase capacity perhaps five-fold by the end of next year. High returns, however, stem from chip shortages, which have lifted rental prices above where they were last year. Markets seem to expect this situation to wane: the price to rent out Nvidia GB300 silicon is about $10 an hour for the next several months, analysts at MoffettNathanson estimated, but only $4 further in the future. If AI demand is lower than expected, or chief clients like Anthropic are stretched too thin, prices could plummet lower. If becoming a cloud operator is just an adolescent phase for SpaceX, then what’s next? There’s always enterprise software, like the promised “Macrohard,” an AI platform to augment workers. The company’s satellite broadband business threatens to take on [USN:L6N4511C3 TEXT:"wireless networks"] worldwide. And SpaceX is building a $17 billion, 100-million-square foot plant for fabricating semiconductors with partner Tesla (TSLA.O) . If Musk chose to [USN:L6N42B10Y TEXT:"jam together"] the two companies fully, cars and robots are added to the menu. Rockets, ironically, fade into obscurity. Revenue for SpaceX’s namesake business grew only 6% compared to last year. It is simply too small to justify such a wild valuation, which was 94 times estimated earnings over the next year before quarterly figures were released. Yet the company [USN:L6N41315K TEXT:"dominates the market"] for putting stuff into orbit, while electric vehicles are beset by rising Chinese rivals, some 200 companies build AI data centers for hire, and countless robot developers pop up. Endless opportunity beckons, just not in the places where SpaceX is actually mature. Follow Robert Cyran on Bluesky . SpaceX said on October 20 that it generated $14.6 billion of revenue in the third quarter, compared to $5.6 billion in the same period a year prior. The company’s Super Intelligence segment produced revenue of $7.6 billion, up from $813 million a year ago. The company earned $4.4 billion of net income, as opposed to a $1.1 billion loss a year ago. Capital expenditures nearly tripled to $19.6 billion, as the company invested $16.4 billion in Super Intelligence. CONTEXT-NEWS

Markets and economies around the world are taking the global energy shock in their stride, but if that's because they're expecting prices to fall any time soon, they may have to readjust. Oil prices closed lower on Tuesday, but not before Brent and WTI crude futures clocked fresh six-month peaks — Brent nudged $112/barrel and WTI rose above $110. It seems a lifetime ago, but when the US and Iran signed the MOU in June, an end to the war, opening of the Strait of Hormuz, and replenishing of global energy supplies seemed imminent. WTI's year-on-year price change even briefly turned negative. But now, WTI is nearly 80% more expensive than it was a year ago and inflationary pressures, although supply-driven, are increasingly difficult for policymakers to look through. Elice shares debuted in Seoul on Tuesday and plunged 32%, the worst debut ever in South Korea for a company that raised more than $100 million in an IPO. Iren shares have lost almost 50% in the past month, CoreWeave and Nebius have both fallen 35% in two weeks. Testing times, but UBS analysts are more sanguine. "A financially stressed neocloud could still own economically valuable assets... That is why we need to look beyond any individual neocloud and examine the broader demand picture." Which, they say, remains robust. 20-year itch If yields are high enough, investors will want a piece of them. Demand won't be anywhere near as strong, with the BTC ratio at auctions over the past year ranging between 2.36 and 2.86, according to Wrightson ICAP. It could even be one of the last 20-year auctions, as speculation mounts that Treasury could scrap them as part of its push to shorten the maturity profile of the debt. item.title: Colts add WR Mecole Hardman Jr., P Thomas Morstead to practice squad
item.description: The Indianapolis Colts signed two veteran players, wide receiver Mecole Hardman Jr. and punter Thomas Morstead, to their practice squad on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Indianapolis Colts signed two veteran players, wide receiver Mecole Hardman Jr. and punter Thomas Morstead, to their practice squad on Tuesday. The Colts also released rookie wide receiver Eli Pancol from the practice squad. He originally was signed to the practice squad on Nov. 18, 2025, and re-signed on Sept. 23. Hardman, 28, played in two games last season for the Buffalo Bills. He did not record a reception on his one target. He returned two punts for 4 yards and one kickoff for 61 yards. A Pro Bowl selection and second-team All-Pro (return specialist) as a rookie in 2019, Hardman has 178 career catches for 2,302 yards and 16 touchdowns, as well as 26 rushing attempts for 190 yards and three TDs in 82 regular-season games (28 starts) with the Kansas City Chiefs (2019-24), New York Jets (2023) and Bills (2025). He has returned 91 punts for 823 yards and one touchdown, and 46 kickoffs for 1,134 yards and one TD. Hardman won three Super Bowl titles with the Chiefs in the 2019, 2022 and 2023 seasons. Kansas City selected Hardman in the second round of the 2019 NFL Draft out of Georgia. Morstead, 40, played last season for the San Francisco 49ers and punted 44 times for a 43.6-yard average in 17 games. He has played for five teams and averaged 46.7 yards on 1,004 punts in 272 games over 17 seasons. Morstead was a Pro Bowl selection in 2012 with the New Orleans Saints. New Orleans selected Morstead in the fifth round of the 2009 draft out of SMU. The Saints won the Super Bowl that season. He played 12 seasons in New Orleans and then moved on to the Jets (2021, 2023-24), Atlanta Falcons (2021), Miami Dolphins (2022) and 49ers (2025). Pancol, 26, has not appeared in an NFL game. --Field Level Media

item.content:encoded: The Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs are co-favorites to win the title as they close out the opening day of the 2026-27 NBA regular season in San Antonio on Tuesday night. BetMGM is offering the Western Conference rivals at +260 to win the title. The Spurs' odds have shifted slightly from opening at +270 to match the Thunder by opening day. Philadelphia opened as a +6000 long shot, but those odds shifted significantly following the trade for Brown and the free-agent signing of James. Going a bit in the opposite direction have been the reigning champion New York Knicks, who are now +1000 after opening at +700. item.title: South Carolina opens at No. 1 in preseason Top 25 poll
item.description: South Carolina is atop the rankings at No. 1 in The Associated Press preseason Top 25 women's basketball poll released Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Carolina is atop the rankings at No. 1 in The Associated Press preseason Top 25 women's basketball poll released Tuesday. The Gamecocks received 23 of 31 first-place votes and 764 points from a national media panel. No. 2 UConn (746 points) earned six first-place votes and No. 3 Southern California (668) had two. Duke (647) and Michigan (644) rounded out the top five. South Carolina coach Dawn Staley's program is the preseason No. 1 for the fifth time in the past seven seasons. "It's a gift and curse," Staley told the AP. "I tend to not look at the number, but our players do. They look at it and feel like there's a sense of respect to being No. 1. "They also know that it's pressure-packed with the type of non-conference schedule we have, we're going to be challenged. If we stand there at No. 1 at the end of our nonconference season, that's something to truly be proud of." South Carolina (36-4 last season) was routed 79-51 by UCLA in last season's title game. UConn (38-1) also reached the Final Four before falling 62-48 to South Carolina. The Huskies have been ranked in the top 10 of every preseason AP poll since 1994. USC (18-14) has high hopes after getting star JuJu Watkins back. She sustained a serious knee injury in the 2025 NCAA Tournament and missed all of last season. After the top five, Texas checks in at No. 6, followed by Louisville, Vanderbilt, LSU and Iowa. Defending champion UCLA is No. 11. The Bruins set records for five first-round picks and six overall players selected from one school in the WNBA Draft. The Big Ten has a record nine teams in the preseason rankings. item.title: Ingresos de SpaceX se disparan y superan las previsiones gracias al auge del negocio de IA
item.description: SpaceX , la empresa de Elon Musk, comunicó el martes un aumento del 161% de sus ingresos del tercer trimestre, que superó las previsiones, impulsado por el auge de su negocio de inteligencia artificial (IA) y el crecimiento constante de su unidad de Internet por satélite Starlink.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: SpaceX (SPCX.O) , la empresa de Elon Musk, comunicó el martes un aumento del 161% de sus ingresos del tercer trimestre, que superó las previsiones, impulsado por el auge de su negocio de inteligencia artificial (IA) y el crecimiento constante de su unidad de Internet por satélite Starlink. Los ingresos del tercer trimestre fueron de 14.600 millones de dólares, frente a la estimación de analistas de 12.720 millones, según datos recopilados por LSEG. Starlink y las operaciones de conectividad en general de SpaceX han sido el principal motor financiero de la empresa, respaldando las ambiciones en materia de IA de Elon Musk. Sin embargo, el software de IA propio de SpaceX, incluido Grok de xAI, se ha visto hasta ahora eclipsado por sus rivales OpenAI, Anthropic y Google (GOOGL.O) . SpaceX obtiene sus ingresos por IA principalmente alquilando capacidad de centros de datos a desarrolladores como Anthropic, Google y Reflection AI, más que a través de sus propios modelos, una operación algo más cercana a la de un proveedor de servicios en la nube que a un laboratorio de IA. El negocio de IA de la empresa abarca Grok, la plataforma de redes sociales X y una operación de centros de datos de rápido crecimiento. El negocio obtiene ingresos de contratos de computación con Anthropic, Google de Alphabet (GOOGL.O) y Reflection AI. Las pérdidas operativas de la unidad de IA han sido considerables y SpaceX ha advertido de que necesitará una inversión sostenida antes de poder generar beneficios de forma constante. La unidad de Internet por satélite ha seguido ampliando su base de abonados, gracias a los lanzamientos de más satélites y a una gama cada vez mayor de servicios para consumidores, empresas, aviación, sector marítimo y administración pública. La empresa ha señalado que la expansión geográfica más allá de los países más ricos podría hacer que los ingresos medios por usuario disminuyeran con el tiempo. Los inversores están muy interesados en saber si esa presión sobre los precios ha comenzado a manifestarse a medida que SpaceX se introduce en más mercados internacionales y lanza planes a precios más bajos. Los inversores también están atentos a si SpaceX puede seguir creciendo al tiempo que mejora la rentabilidad de su red. La empresa está realizando importantes inversiones en cobertura, capacidad y servicios móviles directos al dispositivo. Los inversores también estarán ansiosos por conocer los comentarios de Musk sobre una posible fusión entre SpaceX y Tesla (TSLA.O) , que publicará sus resultados el miércoles.

item.title: Super Micro sees quarterly revenue soaring on AI server boom
item.description: Super Micro Computer expects quarterly revenue and profit margin well above Wall Street estimates as it benefits from relentless AI data center demand, the server maker said on Tuesday, sending shares 11.3% higher in after-hours trading.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Super Micro Computer (SMCI.O) expects quarterly revenue and profit margin well above Wall Street estimates as it benefits from relentless AI data center demand, the server maker said on Tuesday, sending shares 11.3% higher in after-hours trading. Rivals Dell (DELL.N) and HPE (HPE.N) gained between 3.5% and 4.9%. Nvidia (NVDA.O) , the AI chip giant, was up 1.5%. Big Tech's race to build out data centers has placed firms such as Super Micro among the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom. Microsoft, Google, Amazon and Meta are expected to spend more than $700 billion on AI infrastructure this year. That is showing up in Super Micro's results. FORECAST FOLLOWS AI SELLOFF Shares of companies exposed to the AI data-center buildout fell last week after CoreWeave’s (CRWV.O) [USN:L4N46111C TEXT:"stock and bond slide"] and prospects of higher interest rates triggered concerns that heavily indebted operators could take longer than expected to generate returns. S&P Global said on Monday it [USN:L8N4651G6 TEXT:"estimates"] the world's biggest tech firms are likely to have more AI-linked liabilities than known. Super Micro on Tuesday said it expects revenue between $18.5 billion and $19.5 billion in the first quarter, compared with analysts’ average estimate of $15.23 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. That expectation is also well above the company’s prior revenue forecast of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion. The server maker also now expects gross margins to be in the range of 12% to 12.5% versus the prior expectation of 10.4% to 10.8%, and above analysts' estimate of 10.15%, primarily due to customer and product mix. Super Micro last week [USN:L4N4611AO TEXT:"appointed"] former Western Digital (WDC.O) executive Mark Long as its chief financial officer, nearly two years after beginning its search amid [USN:L4N3KE12G TEXT:"scrutiny"] of its financial and accounting practices.

item.title: Commanders WR Terry McLaurin (knee) out for the season
item.description: Washington Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin will miss the rest of the season because of a torn patellar tendon in his left knee, coach Dan Quinn said Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Washington Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin will miss the rest of the season because of a torn patellar tendon in his left knee, coach Dan Quinn said Tuesday. McLaurin was carted off the field late in the first quarter of the Commanders' 23-17 loss against the San Francisco 49ers on Monday night in Santa Clara, Calif. He was running a pass route to the sideline, covered by cornerback Deommodore Lenoir, when he went down under minimal contact and grabbed at his knee. He was eventually fitted with an air cast and driven off the field. An MRI in Washington on Tuesday confirmed the team's fears of the severity of the injury. "Man, he brings a lot on and off the field," Quinn said. "It's a big hit and we'll lean on a number of guys." McLaurin ended the night with one catch for 27 yards, which helped set up a field goal. In five games this season (all starts), the team captain has 15 receptions on 27 targets for one touchdown and a team-leading 230 yards. He didn't play in the Commanders' Oct. 4 loss against the Indianapolis Colts in London due to a hamstring injury, but he was back the following week to make four catches for 62 yards in a tie against the visiting New York Giants. The 31-year-old veteran is in his eighth NFL season, all with Washington, which selected him in the third round of the 2019 draft out of Ohio State. In 112 NFL games (all starts), McLaurin has 513 receptions for 7,191 yards and 42 touchdowns. The two-time Pro Bowl selection is in the first year of a three-year, $96 million contract after signing an extension before the 2025 season. According to reports, the remaining two years have salary-cap hits of $34 million and $39.5 million, with no fully guaranteed future salary. The team could release him after this season or restructure the contract, with Washington saving about $8.5 million against the cap next year if he is released, ESPN reported. On April 1, $5.35 million of McLaurin's salary in 2027 becomes fully guaranteed, according to Spotrac. The Commanders (1-4-1) have a bye week before they return to action with another prime-time game on Nov. 1 against the visiting Philadelphia Eagles (2-4). --Field Level Media

item.title: LATAM dice aumento de capacidad se perfila hacia límite inferior previsto por elevado precio combustible
item.description: LATAM Airlines prevé que el aumento de su capacidad este año se sitúe en la parte inferior del rango previsto tras reducir parte de la oferta en respuesta al alto precio del combustible para aviones, dijo el martes a Reuters su CEO, Roberto Alvo, lo que indica una senda de expansión más cautelosa para el mayor grupo aéreo regional.
item.dc:creator: Kylie Madry
item.content:encoded: LATAM Airlines prevé que el aumento de su capacidad este año se sitúe en la parte inferior del rango previsto tras reducir parte de la oferta en respuesta al alto precio del combustible para aviones, dijo el martes a Reuters su CEO, Roberto Alvo, lo que indica una senda de expansión más cautelosa para el mayor grupo aéreo regional. La aerolínea anunció en agosto que preveía un alza de capacidad del 9-10% interanual en 2026 y un EBITDA ajustado de entre 4.100 y 4.400 millones de dólares. "Hemos cancelado algo más de capacidad debido a los altos precios del combustible", dijo Alvo en una entrevista al margen de la conferencia de la Asociación Latinoamericana y Caribeña de Transporte Aéreo. Según explicó, el modelo de LATAM se mantiene sólido gracias al estricto control de costos y a los mayores ingresos por primas, aunque el grupo, al igual que otras aerolíneas, no ha podido trasladar a los pasajeros la totalidad del avance del costo de combustible. Alvo afirmó que la firma consume entre 36 y 38 millones de barriles anuales de combustible para aviones, lo que significa que una variación de 10 dólares por barril se traduce en un impacto económico anual de aproximadamente 370 millones de dólares. Según explicó, los cálculos en los que se basaban las previsiones anteriores de la compañía ya implicaban unos 1.700 millones de dólares en costos adicionales de combustible para el año, y que el impacto había aumentado ligeramente desde entonces, ya que los precios del cuarto trimestre se mantuvieron por encima de esas estimaciones. Alvo afirmó que el impulso de LATAM hacia el tráfico premium de mayor rentabilidad era una estrategia a largo plazo, más que una respuesta a corto plazo a la crisis del combustible, basada en inversiones en cabinas, salones, servicio a bordo, conectividad y una experiencia del cliente más amplia. También dijo que la firma estaba interesada en estudiar ofrecer servicios a otras ciudades mexicanas, como los centros de negocios de Guadalajara y Monterrey, aunque dichas rutas dependerían en parte de la disponibilidad de aeronaves. Alvo dijo que esas oportunidades podrían volverse más viables a medida que LATAM comience a recibir aviones Airbus A321XLR (AIR.PA) a partir del próximo año.

item.title: Paris game to go forward with heightened security amid unrest
item.description: A game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the New Orleans Saints in Paris on Sunday will go ahead as planned with ramped up security, the NFL said on Tuesday, after a weekend of violence that engulfed the French capital.
item.dc:creator: Amy Tennery
item.content:encoded: A game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the New Orleans Saints in Paris on Sunday will go ahead as planned with ramped up security, the NFL said on Tuesday, after a weekend of violence that engulfed the French capital. French officials will mount a "massive" security operation for protests planned on Saturday, with troops reinforcing police, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said [USN:S8N42Q0F9 TEXT:"on Tuesday"], after rioting and looting swept through Paris and other French cities on October 17. "We always have a very strong security presence," said Peter O'Reilly, the NFL's executive vice president of club business, international and league events. "That presence will be heightened with local authorities (as we are) making sure that there's nothing more important from our standpoint than team security, fan security (and) everybody involved with this game." The Steelers-Saints game will take place at the Stade de France. It is the first regular season game that the league has ever held in the French capital, part of a [USN:L6N44U08L TEXT:"record nine-game slate"] of international matches this season, as the NFL eyes lucrative [USN:L6N41R14V TEXT:"global markets"]. O'Reilly said that the NFL is considering adding a 10th international game to the season beginning in 2027. The violence over the weekend, some of the [USN:L8N46401O TEXT:"worst unrest"] France has suffered in years, followed weeks of largely peaceful [USN:L8N45U0FD TEXT:"student demonstrations"] over school conditions and the cost of living. French authorities instituted curfews in several cities [USN:FWN4630KA TEXT:"on Monday"]. NFL officials have been on the ground in Paris for 10 days, O'Reilly told reporters. "We feel confident that we would not have any impact on the broader resources needed," he said. "That's always top of mind for us and we feel confident that we wouldn't be depleting resources in a negative way around this game."

item.title: Lobbyist sues over ban from consumer product agency, cites law firms' wins in Trump cases
item.description: A Washington lobbyist sued the US Consumer Product Safety Commission and its acting chairman on Tuesday, alleging the agency unlawfully barred him from its facilities and retaliated against him over his work for clients.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: A Washington lobbyist sued the US Consumer Product Safety Commission and its acting chairman on Tuesday, alleging the agency unlawfully barred him from its facilities and retaliated against him over his work for clients. Lobbyist Edward Krenik said in his lawsuit in Washington federal court that the consumer product agency accused him of “disruptive” behavior and declared him a threat without justification. Krenik, represented by the conservative-leaning New Civil Liberties Alliance, said a series of rulings against President Donald Trump’s administration bolstered his retaliation claims. He pointed to [USN:L2N3S00O8 TEXT:"court rulings issued last year"] that blocked White House executive orders targeting four law firms and restricted their ability to interact with federal agencies. Krenik also cited another DC federal [USN:L1N46002Z TEXT:"judge’s order"] commanding the White House to restore access to CNN and several other media outlets. The consumer product agency had no immediate comment. Kara Rollins, a lawyer for Krenik, said in a statement, "the right to petition keeps government answerable to the governed, and it means nothing if officials can banish those with whom they disagree.” Krenik, who owns and operates the government affairs firm NorthStar EK LLC, has been a registered lobbyist for more than 23 years. He previously worked as an aide to lawmakers on Capitol Hill. His lawsuit said most of his current work involves advocacy for manufacturers and trade associations before the consumer product agency. He said that on an unnamed client's behalf he had urged Peter Feldman, the agency’s acting chairman, to take certain actions, and had told Feldman he was authorized to take the client's concerns to the White House. The lawsuit said the White House later contacted Feldman and “admonished” him, and that he was told in August that he was prohibited from entering any Consumer Product Safety Commission building. Krenik said a consumer product agency official had accused him in August without evidence of “repeated abusive and disruptive behavior,” including "attempts to contact staff using improper and unauthorized communication channels.” The lawsuit said Krenik as a private lobbyist has no legal obligation to use any specific communication method when contacting a government official. The case is Edward Krenik v. Peter A. Feldman et al, US District Court for the District of Columbia, No. For plaintiff: Kara Rollins and Christian Clase of New Civil Liberties Alliance For defendants: No appearances yet Read more: [USN:L1N46002Z TEXT:"Judge extends White House access for CNN, MS NOW, Politico amid legal fight"] [USN:L6N44F0U5 TEXT:"Trump invokes presidential privilege in lawsuit over law firm orders"] [USN:S0N3SG00I TEXT:"US Supreme Court lets Trump remove consumer product safety commissioners"] [USN:L2N3S00O8 TEXT:"What Republican, Democratic judges said about Trump’s law firm orders"]

item.title: Hedge fund Sachem Head sees room for Ionic shares to surge
item.description: Hedge fund Sachem Head Capital Management said on Tuesday it believes Ionic Digital's stock price can more than double as the former bitcoin miner shifts into digital infrastructure leasing, amid exploding demand for data center power.
item.dc:creator: Svea Herbst-Bayliss
item.content:encoded: Hedge fund Sachem Head Capital Management said on Tuesday it believes Ionic Digital's (IOND.O) stock price can more than double as the former bitcoin miner shifts into digital infrastructure leasing, amid exploding demand for data center power. Ionic was formed out of the bankruptcy restructuring of crypto lender Celsius Network and started trading in July on the Nasdaq stock exchange, where shares are worth around $63. But there is room for the share price to surge to $151 a share, gaining nearly 140%, Sachem Head founder Scott Ferguson said at the 13D Monitor Active-Passive Investor Summit in New York. Sachem Head, along with Oaktree Capital Management and Attestor Capital, participated in a $400 million private placement in June and owns nearly 10% of the company. Sachem Head owns roughly 9.9% of Ionic and Ferguson said the firm will make a regulatory filing to detail its ownership with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Wednesday. Ionic already holds a 10-year triple-net lease in Texas' Ward County with a possible 10 year extension with Nscale, a London-based, vertically integrated AI infrastructure and neocloud company that operates high-density GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) data centers and cloud platforms. Microsoft is the end customer for this site, Ferguson said. An expansion in Ward County and sites in Midland, Texas would help the stock price gain further, he said. "We think management is pretty good," Ferguson said, adding however that his firm, which from time to time pushes target companies to make changes, may become more involved at the company.

item.title: Fecal waste contaminates sinkholes, drinking wells in Mexico's Yucatan, Greenpeace says
item.description: Water from wells and sinkholes in Mexico's Yucatan state that residents use for drinking is contaminated with fecal bacteria, according to a Greenpeace report published on Tuesday, which said nearby pig farms and municipal wastewater were likely sources.
item.dc:creator: Iñigo Alexander
item.content:encoded: Water from wells and sinkholes in Mexico's Yucatan state that residents use for drinking is contaminated with fecal bacteria, according to a Greenpeace report published on Tuesday, which said nearby pig farms and municipal wastewater were likely sources. Greenpeace called for an immediate moratorium on new industrial livestock operations and farm expansions in the state, home to the ancient Maya civilization. "A range of chemical and microbiological indicators reveal a complex mosaic of severe, localized organic pollution," it said. Greenpeace commissioned an independent laboratory to test water at 17 sites near the state capital Merida in August. The sites included household and farm wells, community water points and cenotes, the natural sinkholes that dot the Yucatan peninsula, one of Mexico's most popular tourist destinations. According to the report, every sample showed some degree of contamination likely linked to fecal waste, and several sites appeared heavily polluted. Total coliform bacteria reached the test's upper limit in 16 of 17 samples, and fecal coliforms did so in 13. However, the tests cannot show whether the waste came from people or animals, and leaking septic tanks and municipal sewage may also contribute to contamination. Greenpeace said the results raise "critical accountability questions" about nearby pig farms. The Yucatan state government was not available for comment, while Mexico's national water commission, CONAGUA, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Merida's Association of Pig Farmers also did not respond to Reuters' request for comment. With no above-ground rivers, groundwater is the Yucatan's only freshwater source, and the area's porous limestone bedrock allows pollutants to quickly seep down into the aquifer. The report said about 30% of local residents drink water drawn directly from wells and sinkholes. Greenpeace, citing its 2020 survey, said only 22 of 257 pig farms in Yucatan had an environmental impact study in place. It also found 43 such farms operating inside protected natural areas. A UN report published in July found that there are over 500 industrial pig farms across Yucatan state with over 50,000 animals, many located near the lands and territories of Indigenous Peoples. Marcos Orellana, the former UN Special Rapporteur who authored the report, said waste and chemicals from industrial farms "find their way very quickly" to water that communities use for bathing, cooking and drinking. He said most farms lack required permits and that regional government initiatives "remain insufficient." "The contamination of the waters that have sustained Mayan culture for millennia is predominantly coming from the industrial operations of the growth of animals," Orellana said. But Antonio Zumarraga, vice president of the Yucatan Citizen Scientific Water Observatory, defended the local pork industry, saying the sector has invested in water treatment and supports conservation programs. He blamed local authorities for lack of action. "It's an issue that, as long as it doesn't carry political weight for the government, they won't do anything about it," Zumarraga said.

item.title: LATAM says capacity growth tracking to lower end of guidance as fuel stays high
item.description: LATAM Airlines expects capacity growth this year to come in at the lower end of its forecast range after trimming some supply in response to high jet fuel prices, Chief Executive Roberto Alvo told Reuters on Tuesday, signaling a more cautious expansion path for Latin America's largest airline group.
item.dc:creator: Kylie Madry
item.content:encoded: LATAM Airlines expects capacity growth this year to come in at the lower end of its forecast range after trimming some supply in response to [USN:L6N45U0HS TEXT:"high jet fuel prices"], Chief Executive Roberto Alvo told Reuters on Tuesday, signaling a more cautious expansion path for Latin America's largest airline group. LATAM said in August it expected [USN:S0N42V03A TEXT:"2026 capacity growth"] of 9% to 10% year over year, and adjusted core earnings of $4.1 billion to $4.4 billion. Alvo said the airline was still tracking within that range, but closer to the bottom end as elevated fuel prices forced some adjustments to planned flying. "We have canceled a little more capacity because of high fuel prices," Alvo said in an interview on the sidelines of the Latin American & Caribbean Air Transport Association conference. He said LATAM's model remained resilient because of strict cost controls and stronger premium revenue, even if the group, [USN:L1N46603J TEXT:"like other airlines"], has been unable to pass through all of the jump in fuel costs to passengers. Alvo said LATAM consumes about 36 million to 38 million barrels of jet fuel a year, meaning a $10-per-barrel move in prices translates into roughly a $370 million annual cost impact. He said the assumptions behind the company's previous guidance already implied about $1.7 billion in additional fuel costs for the year, and that the hit had since grown somewhat as fourth-quarter prices remained above those assumptions. Alvo said LATAM's push toward higher-yield premium traffic was a long-term strategy rather than a short-term response to the fuel shock, built on investments in cabins, lounges, onboard service, connectivity and broader customer experience. He also said LATAM was interested in [USN:L1N46503M TEXT:"studying service"] to additional Mexican cities such as business hubs Guadalajara and Monterrey, although such routes would depend in part on aircraft availability. Alvo said those opportunities could become more viable as LATAM starts receiving Airbus (AIR.PA) A321XLR jets from next year.

item.title: Dow se destaca em Wall Street, com ações do setor de saúde liderando os ganhos
item.description: O Dow subiu 1% nesta terça-feira, superando o índice de referência S&P 500, enquanto o setor de saúde foi o que mais impulsionou Wall Street e o de tecnologia foi o que mais prejudicou o mercado.
item.dc:creator: Sinead Carew, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: O Dow subiu 1% nesta terça-feira, superando o índice de referência S&P 500, enquanto o setor de saúde foi o que mais impulsionou Wall Street e o de tecnologia foi o que mais prejudicou o mercado. O setor de saúde (.SPXHC) liderou os ganhos entre os 11 principais índices setoriais do S&P 500, atingindo uma máxima recorde. A Eli Lilly (LLY.N) foi a empresa que mais contribuiu para o índice S&P 500, enquanto a UnitedHealth (UNH.N) , a MSD & Co (MRK.N) , a Johnson & Johnson (JNJ.N) e a Amgen (AMGN.O) ajudaram a impulsionar o índice Dow Jones de blue chips. As quedas nas ações de megacapitalização puxaram para baixo o setor de serviços de comunicação (.SPLRCL) , enquanto as ações do setor de energia (.SPNY) tiveram desempenho inferior, já que os preços do petróleo caíram após atingirem o maior nível em cinco meses. Os operadores do mercado de petróleo avaliavam uma reunião entre o presidente iraniano e o chefe do Exército do Paquistão — um importante mediador entre os EUA e o Irã —, em contraste com os ataques houthis à infraestrutura saudita e relatos de ataques a embarcações no Golfo. AÇÕES DO SETOR DE TECNOLOGIA DÃO UMA PAUSA Embora o setor de tecnologia de grande peso (.SPLRCT) tenha recuado 0,3%, esse foi o maior fator de queda em pontos do índice S&P 500 e manteve o Nasdaq praticamente estável. As ações de tecnologia haviam se recuperado na segunda-feira após uma onda de vendas na semana passada, quando os investidores se preocuparam com os altos custos de gastos e financiamento para desenvolvimentos em IA. “Os investidores em ações ainda estão um pouco céticos em relação ao setor de IA e à capacidade de algumas dessas empresas de monetizar seus investimentos, então estamos vendo uma certa rotação para outras áreas do mercado”, disse Jim Baird, diretor de investimentos da Plante Moran Financial Advisors, apontando para os avanços registrados nesta terça-feira nas empresas de pequena capitalização e do setor de saúde. “Os investidores estão buscando outras oportunidades fora do setor de tecnologia, e o setor de saúde é um dos beneficiários disso”, disse ele. O Índice Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) subiu 1,02%, para 52.495,88 pontos, o S&P 500 (.SPX) avançou 0,28%, para 7.712,57 pontos, e o Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) teve variação negativa de 0,02%, para 26.424,82 pontos. O índice de valor do S&P 500 (.IVX) subiu 0,9%, em comparação com uma queda de 0,2% em seu equivalente de crescimento (.IGX) . O índice Russell 2000 de pequenas capitalizações (.RUT) fechou com alta de 1,7%. Com um ganho de 1%, o setor de serviços financeiros (.SPSY) foi o segundo maior impulsionador do índice S&P 500. Os setores defensivos também tiveram desempenho superior, com o setor imobiliário (.SPLRCR) subindo 1,7% e o de serviços públicos (.SPLRCU) registrando alta de 1,2%. Uma queda de 1,7% na Netflix, um recuo de 1,6% na Meta (META.O) e uma perda de 1% na Alphabet, controladora do Google (GOOGL.O) , fizeram com que o índice de serviços de comunicação caísse 0,9%. A SpaceX (SPCX.O) divulgou, após o fechamento do mercado, um lucro no terceiro trimestre que superou as estimativas, impulsionando suas ações em 4% no pós-mercado. A Netflix (NFLX.O) divulgou, após o fechamento do mercado, uma previsão de lucro para o quarto trimestre abaixo do esperado, e suas ações caíam 6%. A Meta e a Tesla (TSLA.O) devem divulgar seus resultados na quarta-feira. As ações da General Motors (GM.N) tombaram 6,8% depois que a montadora sinalizou pressão nos próximos meses devido ao aumento dos custos das matérias-primas e à queda nas vendas de caminhões. A 3M (MMM.N) ssubiu 5,8% depois que a empresa anunciou que estava ampliando sua parceria de data centers com a Amazon (AMZN.O) e emitiu um warrant a uma subsidiária da Amazon para a compra de ações ordinárias da 3M no valor de mais de US$521 milhões. O conglomerado industrial também elevou sua previsão de lucro para o ano inteiro. A empresa de relatórios de crédito Equifax (EFX.N) disparou 11,3% após divulgar lucro no terceiro trimestre acima das estimativas dos analistas. As ações da Hasbro (HAS.O) saltaram 11,2% depois que a fabricante de brinquedos elevou sua previsão para o ano inteiro tanto para a receita geral quanto para seu negócio de jogos digitais.

item.title: Lyon omission in the spotlight as Australia seamers endure tough day
item.description: Australia quick Mitchell Starc claimed his 450th test wicket on Tuesday but South Africa's lower order exposed the tourists' decision to omit spinner Nathan Lyon on day three of the second test.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia quick Mitchell Starc claimed his 450th test wicket on Tuesday but South Africa's lower order exposed the tourists' decision to omit spinner Nathan Lyon on day three of the second test. Starc became only the 10th bowler to reach the milestone when Wiaan Mulder gloved a rising delivery from the 36-year-old to Matt Renshaw as South Africa slipped to 110-6. The home side then turned the tables, seeing off the all-seam attack and the back-up part-timers and making the absence of Lyon more pronounced as they went on to score 425-9 before declaring. It did not help that Josh Hazlewood, who took a career-best 6-49 in helping Australia to an emphatic 214-run victory in last week’s first test, could only bowl after lunch. He was sick on Monday, which meant he had to serve his time in the field on Tuesday before being allowed to bowl. He made little impact in nine overs, however, while captain Pat Cummins went wicketless and Starc finished with 3-89. Scott Boland, who replaced Lyon in the team, took his first five-wicket haul outside of Australia, but the tourists had to use Beau Webster to hold up an end and also turned to three other part-time spinners as South Africa piled on the runs. Lyon would have arguably done a better job of stemming South Africa's free scoring on a day when captain Temba Bavuma notched a career-best 179 to give the hosts the upper hand. "If you know you're going to be a man down from the start, you’re probably going with a different make-up, aren’t you?” Starc said. "But unfortunately Josh had a dodgy prawn or something. He'll have fresh legs for the second innings." Lyon was left to play a supporting role from the sidelines. "He's been around long enough to put his shoes back on and be the team man that he is. He was that man for most of the day today, whether it's down at fine leg running us drinks or tapping us on the back. "I’ve been left out plenty of times and naturally you're disappointed that you don't get to play. He'll get another opportunity," added Starc.

item.title: United Airlines profit outlook well below estimates, hit by fuel costs
item.description: United Airlines on Tuesday forecast fourth-quarter profit well below Wall Street estimates despite expectations for record revenue, as soaring fuel costs were expected to persist, eating into gains from strong travel demand and higher ticket prices.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Singh
item.content:encoded: United Airlines (UAL.O) on Tuesday forecast fourth-quarter profit well below Wall Street estimates despite expectations for record revenue, as soaring fuel costs were expected to persist, eating into gains from strong travel demand and higher ticket prices. Airline fares are rising sharply, but fuel costs are climbing even faster, squeezing profits industry wide. With the Iran war threatening to keep fuel prices elevated into 2027, analysts say carriers may have to raise fares further and risk losing customers, or limit flight growth to support ticket prices and protect profits. Earlier this month, United's [USN:L4N45U1TW TEXT:"rival Delta Air Lines"] (DAL.N) cut its annual earnings forecast by nearly a quarter after projecting a $6 billion increase in its fuel bill from last year. Delta CEO Ed Bastian warned that airlines may need to further restrain flight growth next year to sustain higher fares and protect profitability. United expects to pay $4.80 a gallon for jet fuel in the fourth quarter, about 45 cents more than the market consensus assumption. The difference translates into roughly $1 per share in earnings, the company said. The Chicago-based carrier expects adjusted earnings of 50 cents to $1.50 per share for the December quarter. LSEG data shows an average analyst estimate of $1.76. The $1 midpoint of the carrier's outlook is 43% below expectations. Alaska Air Group (ALK.N) added to the industry's warnings on Tuesday, forecasting a fourth-quarter adjusted loss of $2 to $2.50 per share, compared with analyst expectations for a $1.04 loss. The carrier expects its fuel bill for the year to run $1.8 billion above its original plan. Alaska's third-quarter revenue rose 14%, yet its adjusted pretax margin narrowed to 1.1% from 4.6% a year earlier. It expects revenue per unit of capacity to grow by a low-double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter, despite projecting a substantial loss. HIGHER FARES, THINNER MARGINS United's third-quarter results show how soaring fuel costs are eating into gains from higher fares. Its additional fuel spending was equivalent to nearly 70% of the increase in quarterly revenue. Despite record sales, adjusted pretax profit fell and its margin narrowed to 6.2% from 8% a year earlier. Demand, however, remains strong. United carried a record number of passengers, with revenue from business travelers, premium cabins and basic economy all growing at double-digit rates. The airline generated significantly more revenue without substantially increasing flying capacity. The squeeze extends across the industry. US air fares rose an average of nearly 23% year-on-year in the seven months through September, according to Labor Department data. The industry's fuel bill, however, has been climbing even faster. US airlines spent $42.9 billion on fuel in the first eight months of 2026, up $13.2 billion from a year earlier despite slightly lower consumption, government data showed. Analysts at Deutsche Bank have warned that further fare increases could weaken demand, forcing airlines to slow flight growth to support ticket prices. The pressure is spreading beyond the United States. Ryanair (RYA.I) CEO Michael O'Leary [USN:L6N4660EL TEXT:"warned"] on Tuesday that European airfares could rise as much as 20% next year as higher fuel costs and reduced airline capacity squeeze the industry. United and Alaska Air will discuss their financial results in separate calls with analysts and investors on Wednesday morning.

item.title: Musk calls Tesla-SpaceX merger a 'good idea' as SpaceX posts first profit as a public company
item.description: He has in the past tantalized shareholders with the idea citing growing overlap between the companies.
item.dc:creator: Akash Sriram, Joey Roulette
item.content:encoded: Elon Musk said on Tuesday that a merger of his two companies SpaceX (SPCX.O) and Tesla (TSLA.O) would be "a good idea" and that they had formed special committees to discuss a union, sending shares of the space and technology company up 4.9% in extended trading. The company earlier posted its first profit as a public company and Musk said it was tracking an annual revenue run rate of up to $1 trillion. Musk has in the past tantalized shareholders with the idea, [USN:L6N43O1D8 TEXT:"citing growing overlap"] between the companies. Speculation about SpaceX buying the EV maker has [USN:L6N46612X TEXT:"gained traction"] recently, with Barclays suggesting last week that a deal could be announced before Tesla's annual meeting in December. "I think it would be a good idea, but it's really up to the special committees of both companies," Musk said in the first official confirmation that the companies were formally talking. "Because I'm a conflicted party, I can't actually be in the discussion of the special committees," he told investors on a conference call. Shareholders ultimately would need to approve a deal, he added. SpaceX's revenue climbed 161% to $14.58 billion for the three months ended September 30 from a year earlier. AI revenue surged by almost 10 times to $7.56 billion, mostly from renting out data-center capacity to developers such as Anthropic, Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) Google and Reflection AI rather than from its own models. "We are in an inflection moment for SpaceX across launch, connectivity and superintelligence," Musk said on the call. He ended his portion of prepared remarks with a seemingly off-script remark: "In a nutshell, what this implies for SpaceX annual recurring revenue by the end of '27 is somewhere between $500 billion and a trillion." The third quarter offered the clearest evidence yet that SpaceX’s heavy investment in AI is translating into revenue, even as spending on compute infrastructure remains enormous — capital expenses nearly tripled. The shift is reshaping a company whose financial engine has long been its Starlink internet services business and whose longer-term ambitions still hinge on getting Starship rockets into regular service. For now, though, its main business looks closer to a cloud provider's than an AI lab's. AI REVENUE DRIVES SPACEX TRANSFORMATION SpaceX's chief financial officer, Bret Johnsen, reiterated that SpaceX expects annual recurring revenue of about $100 billion by the end of 2026. He said the company expects $35 billion to $40 billion in capital expenditures in the fourth quarter. AI took $16.4 billion of the company's $19.6 billion in capital spending in the third quarter. "SpaceX delivered the quarter the bulls wanted, at least on the top line," said Will Rhind, CEO of asset manager GraniteShares. "The story now is all about AI. The compute contracts signed earlier this year are turning into revenue faster than a lot of people thought." The company's AI business spans Grok, social media platform X and a fast-growing data-center operation. Operating losses at the AI unit have been large and SpaceX has cautioned it will need sustained investment before it can consistently generate profits. But it turned a profit in the third quarter, compared with a year-ago loss.
