item.title: Monedas cotizan dispares; plazas en Brasil ganan con atención a balotaje presidencial
item.description: Las principales monedas de América Latina cotizaron dispares el martes, con algunas perdiendo fuerza incluso en medio de un descenso del dólar a nivel global, mientras los mercados de Brasil avanzaron en medio de posicionamientos previos al balotaje presidencial del domingo.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Farías
item.content:encoded: Las principales monedas de América Latina cotizaron dispares el martes, con algunas perdiendo fuerza incluso en medio de un descenso del dólar a nivel global, mientras los mercados de Brasil avanzaron en medio de posicionamientos previos al balotaje presidencial del domingo. * El dólar descendió en línea con una caída de los precios del petróleo y de los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de más largo plazo, mientras los operadores evaluaban el impacto del aumento de la tensión en la guerra de Estados Unidos con Irán y la sostenibilidad de las fuertes entradas de capital hacia las empresas estadounidenses de IA. * El real brasileño ganó un 0,58% a 5,0182 por dólar, con el mercado atento al balotaje presidencial. Mientras, el referencial bursátil Bovespa (.BVSP) escaló preliminarmente un 1,43% a 208.017 puntos, con datos mostrando flujos de inversores extranjeros hacia las acciones locales antes de la segunda vuelta de la elección del fin de semana. * Los sondeos muestran una estrecha carrera entre el senador de derecha Flávio Bolsonaro y el presidente de izquierda Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, aunque la mayoría de las pesquisas dan una leve ventaja para Bolsonaro, quien ganó la primera vuelta pese a que las encuestas daban ventaja al mandatario. * El peso mexicano cotizaba estable camino al cierre, a 18,4194 unidades por dólar, después de moverse entre alzas y bajas aunque en un rango estrecho. * A nivel local, los inversionistas asimilaban cifras preliminares que mostraron que la [USN:S0N45D031 TEXT:"actividad económica"] se expandió un 3,7% en septiembre a tasa interanual. * En tanto, el índice S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) , integrado por las 35 acciones más líquidas del mercado, cedió parte de sus fuertes alzas de más temprano y ganó un 0,38%, a 69.272,14, marcando su cuarta sesión seguida de avances en medio de los primeros resultados corporativos del tercer trimestre. * El peso chileno , cerró las operaciones con un alza del 0,68%, a 974,20/974,50 por dólar, y alcanzó su mayor nivel de cierre en dos semanas, impulsado por el retroceso del billete verde en los mercados globales. * Asimismo, el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA (.SPIPSA) , revirtió un avance previo y retrocedió un 0,42%, a 10.926,50 puntos. * El peso colombiano borró ganancias iniciales y finalizó con caída de un 0,51% a 3.174 unidades por dólar; mientras que en la bolsa el índice accionario MSCI COLCAP (.COLCAP) subió un 0,47% a 2.533,22 puntos. * El peso interbancario argentino cedió un 0,03% a 1.525 por dólar con intervención cotidiana del banco central (BCRA), que supera compras por 15.600 millones de dólares en el transcurso del 2026. La entidad adquirió 103 millones de dólares el martes. * La Secretaría de Finanzas argentina realizaba durante la jornada una conversión de títulos para ofrecer a modo de canje anticipado y reducir la potencial volatilidad cambiaria antes de la fijación del precio el 27 de octubre. * El índice accionario MSCI Merval (.MMXMRVLGA) de la bolsa de Buenos Aires, en tanto, cayó un 0,17% al cierre, tras una jornada de fuerte volatilidad luego escalar más de un 1% durante la sesión. En la rueda previa se hundió un 1,84%. * La moneda peruana, el sol , cedió leves alzas iniciales y finalizó estable a 3,4250/3,4270 unidades por dólar. Por su parte, la Bolsa de Lima (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) perdió fuerza y cerró con una mínima alza del 0,03% a 1.579,07 puntos.

item.title: US coaxing refiners to produce more diesel as prices surge, energy officials say
item.description: Two top US Energy Department officials said on Tuesday they were working with refiners at home and abroad to boost fuel output as a diesel shortage has raised prices, driving dissatisfaction among voters with the White House ahead of the November midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Crooks, Arathy Somasekhar
item.content:encoded: Two top US Energy Department officials said on Tuesday they were working with refiners at home and abroad to boost fuel output as a diesel shortage has raised prices, driving dissatisfaction among voters with the White House ahead of the November [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"]. Diesel prices have jumped to record highs because of disruptions from the Iran war and Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries . Retail diesel prices averaged about $6.32 a gallon on Tuesday, according to motorist group AAA. The Trump administration has taken several steps to try to lower fuel prices that have surged since the start of the Iran war on February 28, including relaxing restrictions on Russian diesel exports, invoking the Defense Production Act to boost output and allowing commercial vehicles to run on red-dyed diesel normally limited to off-road equipment. Diesel is critical to the global economy, powering much of the transport, agriculture and heavy industry that underpin global trade and economic activity. The high cost of fuel has soured voters on US President Donald Trump's stewardship of the economy, with 36% approving of Trump on that issue, according to the most recent Reuters/Ipsos opinion poll . "We are talking about reopening every refinery we can," Energy Secretary Chris Wright said in Houston. "There are dialogues there, and that's a tough challenge. I'm not saying all these are going to happen." DIFFICULT TO RAISE US OUTPUT US refineries are running near full capacity, and with several facilities shutting in recent years, there is little leeway to quickly boost domestic output, analysts say. [USN:L6N3Q20MK TEXT:"Refinery expansions"] are capital intensive and take months, if not years, to complete depending on the complexity of the additions. Wright said the US is also working with India to increase refining output there to bring products to global markets. American Petroleum Institute CEO Mike Sommers told Reuters on the sidelines of an energy forum in Titusville, Pennsylvania that US refiners are running at 95% to 100% of capacity. He said they are putting off planned maintenance because of high prices. “The American refiners are doing everything they can,” Sommers said. He said that using the Defense Production Act to restart idled plants, as the administration has floated, would require a lot of capital. Last week, Vice President JD Vance said the administration would use the Defense Production Act to [USN:L6N45Z1BU TEXT:"expand capacity"] of a Texas refinery owned by Delek US Holdings (DK.N) . Trump signed legislation last year that included $1 billion in Defense Production Act funding for energy-related projects deemed critical to national security. Wright said there was "more to do" on refining and the Defense Production Act but did not provide additional details. Sommers singled out China's spare refining capacity, saying their government is currently barring diesel exports. Beijing “is really going to be the key if we’re going to get long-term prices down,” he said. A spokesperson for the Chinese embassy in Washington said the key to resolving the issue is to achieve a ceasefire in Iran. "China stands ready to maintain communication with all sides to jointly safeguard global energy security and keep industrial and supply chains stable," the spokesperson added. PUSH FOR EUROPEAN DIESEL Trump [USN:S0N43U024 TEXT:"temporarily waived sanctions"] this month on Russian diesel in an attempt to lower prices. Russian diesel will likely move to New England, if it moves to the US at all, Wright said. Already, cargoes from Russia are returning to their[USN:L6N4660PS TEXT:" traditional destinations"] after the US suspended sanctions, with two tankers signaling trips to Turkey and Brazil in recent days, Reuters reported on Tuesday. The Trump administration has also been pushing Europe to release more fuel to balance global markets. "We are working with our friends ... to find new and innovative ways to get more throughput" through refineries, said Energy Department Under Secretary Kyle Haustveit at the Drake Forum in Titusville. While the Trump administration has pushed Europe to release 50 million barrels of diesel, an agreement by industrialized nations fell short of that target. The Paris-based International Energy Agency said last week it would speed the release of crude and oil product volumes pledged in March, including more than 20 million barrels of diesel as soon as possible. Fatih Birol, chief of the IEA, which coordinates industrialized nations' releases of oil from emergency stocks, said on Tuesday the [USN:L6N4660MV TEXT:"group is ready"] to coordinate more oil releases by member countries if needed.

item.title: Riesgo país de Argentina supera 700 puntos básicos, su máximo nivel en un año
item.description: El índice del riesgo país de Argentina renovó el martes su máximo nivel desde finales de octubre del 2025 por una mayor diferencia en las paridades de los bonos soberanos ante los de Estados Unidos, producto de la prudencia inversora de las últimas semanas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El índice del riesgo país de Argentina renovó el martes su máximo nivel desde finales de octubre del 2025 por una mayor diferencia en las paridades de los bonos soberanos ante los de Estados Unidos, producto de la prudencia inversora de las últimas semanas. Este referencial actualizado a diario por el banco J.P. Morgan llegó a trepar a los 710 puntos básicos de manera intradiaria. Junto a una fuerte volatilidad, pasó a reacomodarse luego en torno a los 672 puntos (2000 GMT), contra unas 675 unidades el lunes, su máximo nivel en el último año, una tendencia genérica que preocupa al mercado argentino por el recorte de liquidez. El Gobierno del libertario Javier Milei trata de bajar la efervescencia que esto provoca entre los ahorristas al señalar que la sumatoria de más reservas e intercambio de monedas activados servirían como sostén en caso de cualquier presión financiera extra. "Hay instrumentos que el Gobierno puede activar en caso de una corrida cambiaria, por ejemplo, pero al mercado le incomoda por incremento del costo ver un riesgo país por arriba de los 700 puntos desde los 400 (puntos) logrados a comienzo de julio", dijo un analista de un banco chino que opera en Buenos Aires. La deuda pública extrabursátil promedió una pérdida del 0,2%, con dolarización de carteras y tras el derrumbe del 1,3% el lunes, mientras que el índice accionario MSCI Merval (.MMXMRVLGA) de la bolsa porteña cayó un ligero 0,17% al cierre, tras absorber un alza inicial y contra un debut negativo del 1,84%. Este indicador bursátil renovó su nombre el lunes, otorgando la oportunidad ahora de poder ser comprado como un activo más, al estilo de los grandes índices del mundo y para tener una mayor competitividad frente a los fondos comunes de inversión. Las próximas elecciones presidenciales de Argentina, a finales del 2027, comienzan a generar síntomas de cautela ya que Milei dijo que irá por su reelección, pero la tendencia de las encuestas no tranquiliza los negocios. A esto se suma el riesgo geopolítico global latente, lo que aumenta la aversión al riesgo en general. Al respecto, la consultora Quantum Finanzas dijo que "la suba del petróleo y nuevas dudas sobre la inversión en 'IA' presionan a los futuros de los índices bursátiles estadounidenses". El peso interbancario cedió apenas un 0,03% a 1.525 por dólar con intervención cotidiana del banco central (BCRA), que supera compras por 15.600 millones de dólares en el transcurso del 2026. Estas adquisiciones sumaron 103 millones de dólares este martes. Un reciente informe interno del BCRA indicó que restan cerca de 4.000 millones de dólares por liquidar de emisiones corporativas, con un neto de poco más de 2.000 millones tras descontar pagos de empresas. En octubre, las colocaciones de deuda corporativa y subsoberana suman alrededor de 100 millones de dólares, según operadores. Mientras tanto, la Secretaría de Finanzas llevaba a cabo durante la jornada una conversión de títulos para ofrecer a modo de canje anticipado y reducir la potencial volatilidad cambiaria antes de la fijación del precio el 27 de octubre. Esta negociación permitirá a los tenedores del bono 'dollar-linked' con vencimiento a fin de octubre (D30O6) canjearlo por instrumentos con amortización a fines de noviembre próximo, o en enero y en junio de 2027. El Gobierno viene de reportar superávit en la balanza comercial ([USN:L1N4650UP TEXT:"ICA"]) de septiembre por 2.976 millones de dólares, con exportaciones récord por arriba de los 10.000 millones, mientras el miércoles se conocerá la actividad económica de agosto ([USN:L1N4660KB TEXT:"EMAE"]), en momentos de temor por una potencial recesión en el tercer trimestre del año.

item.title: US FDA issues guidance on apps used with prescription drugs
item.description: The US FDA on Tuesday issued guidance aimed at clarifying how drug companies can develop, distribute and label apps used alongside their prescription medicines.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US FDA on Tuesday issued guidance aimed at clarifying how drug companies can develop, distribute and label apps used alongside their prescription medicines. Here are some details: The policy outlines when content in such apps must be submitted to the US Food and Drug Administration, when those apps should be referenced in a drug's prescribing information, and what information companies need to provide to the health regulator. Apps linked to medical devices, such as software paired with an asthma inhaler, should generally be included in an associated drug's label, the FDA said Standalone apps that track symptoms, provide reminders or offer coaching should be listed in the label only if these apps are essential for the medicine's safe and effective use or offer meaningful clinical benefit, it said In most cases, information displayed to patients through a companion app will be treated as promotional material, in line with the regulator's approach to other forms of drug advertising The FDA said the guidance intends to reduce regulatory uncertainty for drugmakers and technology developers while maintaining safety and effectiveness standards

item.title: Portugal housing protesters return to squares, vow to press on
item.description: Thousands of protesters returned to two central squares in Lisbon and Porto on Tuesday and vowed to press on with demonstrations against Portugal's deepening housing crisis, hours after police cleared tent camps before dawn and made 55 arrests.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Goncalves, Miguel Pereira
item.content:encoded: Thousands of protesters returned to two central squares in Lisbon and Porto on Tuesday and vowed to press on with demonstrations against Portugal's deepening housing crisis, hours after police cleared tent camps before dawn and made 55 arrests. A popular assembly in Lisbon voted on Tuesday evening to return to Rossio square and set up tents again on Wednesday. Singer Ana Moura joined protesters there and performed in support of the movement. Organisers said more than 1,000 people had gathered in each square. Police gave no crowd estimate. Debora Miranda, 41, a communications consultant, told Reuters she joined the Rossio square protest to represent generations struggling with soaring costs. "If people don't feel at home, in every sense of the word, they can't move forward with their lives...enough is enough." Activists had occupied Lisbon's Rossio square since Saturday, pitching around 200 tents, and Porto's Dom Joao I square for around 10 days. The camps mirrored housing protests in [USN:L1N45U0F8 TEXT:"neighbouring Spain"], and coincided with unrest over rising living costs in countries such as [USN:L6N4650BY TEXT:"France"], [USN:L6N46303L TEXT:"Belgium"] and [USN:L8N463090 TEXT:"Italy"]. Shortly before 6 a.m., after warning protesters that the camps were illegal, police launched coordinated operations in both cities. The protesters took down their own tents in Porto while officers cleared Rossio square. Carla Valadao, a spokesperson for the Lisbon camp, described the police operation as "very aggressive". Public Security Police superintendent Sergio Soares told reporters that the eviction had been "calm, proportionate and appropriate, with no police charge". The 55 detainees were later released pending a court appearance in Lisbon on Wednesday. Portugal is grappling with one of Europe's worst housing affordability crises. Purchase prices have more than doubled since 2017 and rents for new leases have nearly doubled. The squeeze is most acute in the major cities, where there has also been opposition to excessive tourism and an influx of so-called digital nomads. The protesters are demanding the centre-right government withdraw a [USN:L6N45M1AX TEXT:"bill"] making evictions easier and ending rent caps on new leases, which passed a first parliamentary reading with the abstention of the far-right Chega party. Jorge Paixao, 19, a history student, called it "a societal crisis", saying his generation needed "the ability to live with dignity, start families and rejuvenate Portugal."

item.title: Ormat dominates US geothermal auction in Nevada
item.description: A Trump administration sale of geothermal energy leases in Nevada attracted nearly $4.5 million in winning bids on Tuesday, with developers Ormat and Invenergy as the top spenders.
item.dc:creator: Nichola Groom
item.content:encoded: A Trump administration sale of geothermal energy leases in Nevada attracted nearly $4.5 million in winning bids on Tuesday, with developers Ormat (ORA.N) and Invenergy as the top spenders. The auction drew bids on 60 of the 83 land parcels offered by the Interior Department's Bureau of Land Management, according to sale results posted on a government web site. Those 69 leases cover 186,641 acres in the state. The sale was the fourth of six government geothermal auctions held in 2026 and the first this year in Nevada, which boasts substantial geothermal resources. President Donald Trump's administration has [USN:L1N45D0WR TEXT:"promoted"] [USN:S0N3RO0B5 TEXT:"geothermal"] energy as a promising new source of always-on electricity that can help meet the nation's soaring demand for electricity tied to the expansion of artificial intelligence. Ormat, an established geothermal developer with substantial holdings in Nevada, accounted for nearly half of the auction's total high bids, winning eight parcels on about 20,000 acres for $2.29 million. Ormat also placed the auction's highest bid of $201 per acre for a 3,841-acre parcel in White Pine County in eastern Nevada. Invenergy, an energy and infrastructure developer that has recently expanded into geothermal, picked up nine parcels on 37,000 acres for $694,947. The company was the auction's largest winner by acreage. Glovate LLC was the auction's third-biggest winner, claiming six parcels on 24,000 acres for $570,601. It was not immediately known if Glovate, which was formed in Delaware earlier this month, is tied to an established geothermal company. Some of the acreage offered overlapped with major planned solar energy projects. Two parcels that [USN:L1N46117D TEXT:"overlap"] with NextEra Energy's Sawtooth solar project were won by United Minerals and Mining LLC, another entity established in Delaware this month. Geothermal energy has been produced in the United States since the mid-1900s, but it has recently emerged as one of the fastest-growing areas of the power sector as companies have adapted oil-and-gas drilling techniques to tap heat deep underground. Lease prices at government geothermal auctions have soared this year, but competition at the Nevada auction was concentrated in a handful of parcels. More than a third of the leases sold at the minimum price of $2 an acre.

item.title: El Brent cae tras encuentro de mediador pakistaní en Irán
item.description: El petróleo cayó tras alcanzar el martes un pico de cinco meses, mientras los operadores valoraban una reunión entre el presidente iraní y el jefe del ejército de Pakistán -mediador con Estados Unidos-, junto a los ataques hutíes a infraestructura saudí y las noticias sobre buques en el golfo Pérsico.
item.dc:creator: Georgina Mccartney
item.content:encoded: El petróleo cayó tras alcanzar el martes un pico de cinco meses, mientras los operadores valoraban una reunión entre el presidente iraní y el jefe del ejército de Pakistán -mediador con Estados Unidos-, junto a los ataques hutíes a infraestructura saudí y las noticias sobre buques en el golfo Pérsico. Los futuros del crudo Brent cerraron con una caída de 76 centavos, o un 0,69%, a 108,79 dólares. A primera hora de la sesión, el contrato con vencimiento más cercano alcanzó los 111,99 dólares, un máximo en cinco meses. El contrato para noviembre del crudo estadounidense West Texas Intermediate, que venció el martes, cerró con una caída de 1,87 dólares, o un 1,8%, a 101,79 dólares, con un descenso frente al máximo de la sesión, de 110,48 dólares, el más alto desde abril para un contrato cercano. El contrato de diciembre, más activo, cerró con una caída de 72 centavos, a 97,82 dólares el barril. El presidente de Irán, Masoud Pezeshkian, abordó los esfuerzos de mediación y los acontecimientos regionales durante una reunión con el jefe del ejército de Pakistán, el mariscal de campo Asim Munir, en Teherán, según el medio iraní Nournews. Los esfuerzos de mediación de Pakistán dieron lugar a un acuerdo de paz provisional firmado en junio. Sin embargo, se vino abajo rápidamente por los nuevos enfrentamientos entre Irán y Estados Unidos semanas después. Las conversaciones en Teherán ocurren en medio de continuos ataques de los hutíes yemeníes, quienes afirmaron el lunes que habían bombardeado objetivos energéticos, aeroportuarios y militares saudíes, como una instalación de Aramco (2222.SE) en Yanbu, el yacimiento petrolífero de Shaybah, el Aeropuerto Internacional rey Khalid de Riad y el aeropuerto de Abha. Las autoridades saudíes no confirmaron de inmediato las afirmaciones de los hutíes y Reuters no pudo verificarlas de forma independiente. "Los precios del petróleo siguen bien respaldados (...) Esto sugiere que el mercado está descontando una prima de riesgo significativa, dada la volatilidad de la situación", señalaron los analistas de ING en una nota el martes. Al menos 18 buques fueron atacados en el transcurso de dos semanas, lo que mantiene intacta la prima de riesgo, dijo el rastreador de buques Kpler en una nota el lunes.

item.title: TSX rises as drop in oil prices helps lower interest rates
item.description: Canada's main stock index rose on Tuesday, helped by gains for financial and telecommunication stocks, as oil pulled back from its highest level since April and investors looked ahead to a more seasonally favorable period for the market.
item.dc:creator: Fergal Smith
item.content:encoded: Canada's main stock index rose on Tuesday, helped by gains for financial and telecommunication stocks, as oil pulled back from its highest level since April and investors looked ahead to a more seasonally favorable period for the market. The S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) ended up 179.33 points, or 0.5%, at 36,107.96, stopping just short of Friday's closing level, which was the highest in over three weeks. "You are entering one of the best seasonal periods of the year. November and December are historically pretty rewarding months, especially given the current environment that is really oversold from a breadth perspective," said Sid Mokhtari, chief market technician for CIBC Capital Markets. [USN:L1N46601X TEXT:"US crude oil futures"] settled 1.8% lower at $101.79 a barrel as traders weighed a meeting between the Iranian president and Pakistan's army chief, a key US-Iran mediator, against continued Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure. The move in oil helped lower interest rates, said Mokhtari, adding, "you bring rates lower then you start buoying the utilities and telcos — things that were hit hard with the recent rise in rates." The Canadian 10-year yield eased 6.8 basis points to 3.894% after rising sharply on Monday as investors raised bets on a Bank of Canada interest rate hike next week. The communication services index (.GSPTTTS) and heavily weighted financials (.SPTTFS) both rose 1%, while industrials ended 0.7% higher. Shares of [USN:L1N4660P1 TEXT:"Bombardier"] (BBDb.TO) advanced 4.4% after US President Donald Trump dropped threats against the jet maker to ban it from the US market. BlackBerry (BB.TO) was another standout, rising 7.9% and contributing to gains for the technology sector (.SPTTTK) . Resource shares were a drag, with energy (.SPTTEN) falling 0.5% and the materials group (.GSPTTMT) ending 0.8% lower. The price of [USN:L1N4660U8 TEXT:"gold"] was down 0.4%.

item.title: Dow outperforms as Wall Street rises, healthcare stocks lead gains
item.description: The Dow rose 1% on Tuesday, outperforming the benchmark S&P 500 while the healthcare sector provided Wall Street's biggest boost and technology was its biggest drag.
item.dc:creator: Sinead Carew, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: The Dow rose 1% on Tuesday, outperforming the benchmark S&P 500 while the healthcare sector provided Wall Street's biggest boost and technology was its biggest drag. Healthcare (.SPXHC) led gains among the S&P 500's 11 major sector indexes, hitting a record high. Eli Lilly (LLY.N) was the S&P 500's biggest index point contributor while UnitedHealth (UNH.N) , Merck & Co (MRK.N) , Johnson & Johnson (JNJ.N) and Amgen (AMGN.O) helped boost the blue-chip Dow industrials. Declines in megacap stocks pulled down the communication services (.SPLRCL) sector. Energy (.SPNY) shares underperformed as[USN:L1N46601X TEXT:" oil prices"] fell after touching a five-month high. Oil traders were weighing a meeting between the Iranian president and Pakistan's army chief, a US-Iran mediator, against Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf. TECH STOCKS TAKE A BREATHER While the heavyweight technology (.SPLRCT) sector eased 0.3%, it was the biggest index-point drag on the S&P 500 and kept the Nasdaq close to flat. Technology stocks had rebounded on Monday from a selloff last week when investors worried about steep spending and financing costs for AI developments. "Equity investors are still a little skeptical around the AI trade and the ability for some of these companies to monetize their investments, so you're seeing a bit of a rotation into other areas of the market," said Jim Baird, chief investment officer at Plante Moran Financial Advisors, pointing to advances on Tuesday in small caps and healthcare companies. "Investors are looking for other opportunities outside of tech, and healthcare is one of the beneficiaries of that," he said. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 529.85 points, or 1.02%, to 52,495.88, the S&P 500 (.SPX) gained 21.84 points, or 0.28%, to 7,712.57 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) lost 6.07 points, or 0.02%, to 26,424.82. The S&P 500 value index (.IVX) rose 0.9% compared with a 0.2% drop in its growth counterpart (.IGX) . The small-cap Russell 2000 index (.RUT) finished up 1.7%. With a 1% gain, the financial services sector (.SPSY) was the S&P 500's second-biggest index point boost. Defensive sectors also outperformed, with real estate (.SPLRCR) adding 1.7% and utilities (.SPLRCU) climbing 1.2%. A 1.7% drop in Netflix, a 1.6% decline in Meta (META.O) and a 1% loss in Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL.O) sent the communication services index down 0.9%. SpaceX (SPCX.O) reported a [USN:L4N4661M0 TEXT:"third-quarter profit"] after the market closed that blew past estimates, boosting its shares 4% in late trading. Netflix (NFLX.O) issued a [USN:L6N4661BU TEXT:"weaker-than-expected forecast"] for fourth-quarter profit after the bell, and its shares fell 6%. Meta and Tesla (TSLA.O) are scheduled to report on Wednesday. General Motors (GM.N) shares sank 6.8% after the automaker [USN:L6N4660PI TEXT:"signaled pressure in coming months"] from higher commodity costs and lower truck sales. 3M (MMM.N) rose 5.8% after the [USN:L4N4651MW TEXT:"company said"] it was expanding its data-center partnership with Amazon (AMZN.O) and issued a warrant to an Amazon subsidiary to purchase 3M common stock worth over $521 million. The industrial conglomerate also raised its full-year profit forecast. Credit reporting firm Equifax (EFX.N) rallied 11.3% after it reported third-quarter profit above analysts' estimates. Hasbro shares (HAS.O) jumped 11.2% after the toymaker [USN:L6N4660PC TEXT:"raised its full-year forecast"] for both overall revenue and its digital gaming business. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 2.04-to-1 ratio on the NYSE, where there were 114 new highs and 236 new lows. On the Nasdaq, 3,245 stocks rose and 1,608 fell as advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 2.02-to-1 ratio. The S&P 500 posted 22 new 52-week highs and one new low, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 46 new highs and 266 new lows. On US exchanges, 15.91 billion shares changed hands compared with the 17.15 billion average for the last 20 sessions.

item.title: Colombian Congress approves budget allocations, cuts funding to peace deal
item.description: Colombian lawmakers approved spending distributions for next year's 634.9 trillion pesos ($201.14 billion) budget on Tuesday, trimming spending linked to a 10-year-old peace agreement and boosting debt service payments.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Colombian lawmakers approved spending distributions for next year's 634.9 trillion pesos ($201.14 billion) budget on Tuesday, trimming spending linked to a 10-year-old peace agreement and boosting debt service payments. The budget, which projects a 2027 fiscal deficit of 9.4% of gross domestic product, is a significant increase from the 555.8 trillion peso budget for this year. The bill allocates 141 trillion pesos, about $45 billion for debt repayment next year, up from about $30 billion allocated in 2026. Neither congress nor the finance ministry had published a complete breakdown of the approved budget by morning on Tuesday and a congressional source told Reuters a final version could take days, as some modifications were approved by only one of the chambers. The bigger budget comes as Colombia, Latin America's fourth-largest economy, struggles to put its public accounts in order. Public debt is expected to rise this year and next, moving the country further from regaining the investment-grade rating it lost in 2021. The government of new right-wing President Abelardo De La Espriella had promised to trim remaining spending for this year and said it plans to propose a 'Rescue Law' to Congress to cut 2027 spending and reduce the fiscal deficit to 7.2% of GDP. Lawmakers in the lower house approved the bill with 112 votes in favor and only one against it, while in the Senate it passed with 57 votes in favor and one against. Lawmakers had until Tuesday night to pass the budget before it would be possible for the government to put it through via decree. "Thank you all for giving us this vote of confidence. We are going to succeed in getting the country out of this very complex economic situation," Finance Minister Miguel Gomez said after the Senate passed the bill late on Monday night. SPENDING CUTS The budget cuts funds for the Special Jurisdiction for Peace (JEP) - the court created under a 2016 peace deal with the former Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) guerrillas to try rebel leaders and ex-soldiers for war crimes - by some 181 billion pesos, the finance ministry said in a statement, and reassigns that money to the defense ministry. The cut amounts to 23% of the court's budget, an even deeper reduction than had been previously expected. The court has said cuts will [USN:L6N45R12F TEXT:"limit investigations and trials"], make it difficult to provide victims with lawyers, psychological support and travel expenses, and put security schemes to protect victims and former combatants at risk. The operational budget for the Search Unit for Disappeared People, created under the peace deal to look for at least 137,000 people who vanished during the ongoing armed conflict, was cut by nearly 22%. The unit has warned a cut of that magnitude will threaten DNA collection from families and some 10,000 planned exhumations of remains. ($1 = 3,156.50 Colombian pesos)

item.title: US envoy Witkoff to meet Putin, Trump presses Kyiv to settle
item.description: Zelenskiy told a news conference after the Oslo meeting that Ukraine was again receiving early warnings of Russian missile attacks.
item.dc:creator: Nerijus Adomaitis, Lina Golovnya, Steve Holland
item.content:encoded: US envoy Steve Witkoff will meet Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday after what a US official called "constructive" talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy in Norway, as President Donald Trump said it was time for Ukraine to end the war. The US official said Ukraine brought forward new ideas and proposals to the Oslo talks, which also involved the leaders of Norway and Finland and European and NATO representatives, and that participants made "meaningful progress" toward a coordinated approach to engaging Russia. The official, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, said the talks covered "key elements of a comprehensive peace framework," including security guarantees for Ukraine, a post-war economic plan and a broader European security architecture. Witkoff would aim to "create a pathway toward direct trilateral and broader multilateral negotiations," the official said. Zelenskiy travelled to Oslo seeking to repair relations with Washington, which have sunk to new lows as Trump has courted Moscow. Kyiv has complained that Washington has withheld vital military support and intelligence. Zelenskiy told a news conference after the Oslo meeting and an earlier phone call with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio that Ukraine was again receiving early warnings of Russian missile attacks. "Now it works, it's great," he said, adding he and Rubio had discussed supplies of Patriot missile interceptors as well as the satellite-based Starlink system, which Kyiv complained had stopped working when mounted on fast-moving objects such as drones. Trump's recent gestures toward Moscow, including a deal to buy Russian diesel and a waiver of new sanctions, sparked bipartisan pushback in the US Congress and worry in European capitals. Zelenskiy said he had discussed "Article 5-like" security guarantees, referring to the NATO stipulation that an attack on one ally is an attack on all. "I am thankful to the American side that they underlined again that it will be strong," he said. Zelenskiy reiterated that Ukraine hoped to discuss key issues on how to end the war during a trilateral meeting of leaders of Ukraine, Russia and the US. Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere told the news conference the Oslo meeting had been good and constructive, while Finnish President Alexander Stubb added: "I think the (peace) process is back on track." Washington has denied deliberately hindering Ukraine's war effort. But Trump has repeatedly [USN:L6N4611D3 TEXT:"rebuked Zelenskiy"], and called for him to be [USN:L6N45W06G TEXT:"replaced"]. On Tuesday, Trump called on Ukraine to make a deal to settle the war, and said Moscow wanted to get it done. "Ukraine has to want to settle this war," he told reporters. Trump suggested Moscow had the upper hand in the fight because "Russia is a big machine — they just keep grinding forward, and that's what they've done. They've taken a very large piece of land." RUBIO SAYS US MISSILES MAY NOT HAVE BEEN DELIVERED YET The US under Trump has largely stopped providing weapons directly to Ukraine but lets European countries buy US weaponry on Kyiv's behalf under a program known as Prioritised Ukraine Requirements List (PURL). It has also provided intelligence and technology that Europe cannot match. A source familiar with the matter said most weapons deliveries under PURL continued to flow, but US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had not approved Ukraine’s latest requests for Patriot interceptors. Rubio acknowledged on Tuesday that a consignment of interceptors bought by European countries for Ukraine may not have been delivered, but denied that the US had changed policy. "There has not been some deliberate political directive to go out and harm Ukraine," he said on a visit to India. Hegseth told reporters US policy toward Ukraine had not changed and stressed the need to maintain US stockpiles. "Certainly, with things like interceptors, we want to make sure our guys have the most possible as well," he said. He also said Washington had [USN:SPN4650B4 TEXT:"not pulled back Ukraine's ability to access Starlink"], which is owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX, and appeared to signal that the problem rested with corporate terms of service Kyiv needed to comply with. Musk has said Starshield, the military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink communications system, is controlled by the US government and any limits on its use are ultimately up to Trump. Tuesday's Wall Street Journal cited US officials and people familiar with the matter as saying that Musk ordered the slowdown after consulting with Trump and other administration officials. Reuters [USN:L1N4610ZC TEXT:"reported"] earlier that the order to limit the service came from the White House. While US ties with Ukraine have deteriorated, Russia has stepped up attacks on Ukrainian cities, particularly targeting power stations and fuel, despite a call from Trump for both sides to spare each other's energy systems. Russia bombarded cities in western Ukraine overnight, targeting electricity systems and [USN:L1N4660DM TEXT:"knocking out power"] across swathes of the country that had previously been spared. Ukraine held back for several days last week from hitting Russian oil refineries in deference to Trump's request, but has resumed strikes after Russia showed no sign of complying. Both sides have also struck data centres. Trump has repeatedly condemned Ukrainian attacks on Russia while saying little about Russia's far more severe attacks on Ukraine. RUSSIAN ATTACKS Russia's defence ministry said on Tuesday it struck three cargo vessels in Ukraine's port of Reni and two other cargo vessels en route to Odesa. Russian forces also hit two logistics hubs, it said. Energy facilities were attacked in seven Ukrainian regions overnight, knocking out power, and the western Lviv region was struck again during the day. Russian drones also struck an energy facility in Kyiv on Tuesday, mayor Vitali Klitschko said, with authorities saying power was out in four districts. The deterioration of US-Ukraine relations began 10 days ago when Trump lifted sanctions on Russian diesel in a deal agreed with Putin. Trump said this would help reduce high fuel prices that have upset US voters ahead of midterm elections on November 3. At the weekend, Trump issued a broad waiver of tougher sanctions on Russia that were meant to have begun this week.

item.title: Congreso de Colombia aprueba presupuesto de gastos para 2027 por 634,9 billones de pesos
item.description: El Congreso de Colombia aprobó el martes el presupuesto de gastos para 2027 por 634,9 billones de pesos (201.168 millones de dólares), que contempla una reasignación de recursos entre diferentes sectores, un recorte en rubros relacionados con el acuerdo de paz y un incremento de los recursos destinados al pago del servicio de la deuda.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Congreso de Colombia aprobó el martes el presupuesto de gastos para 2027 por 634,9 billones de pesos (201.168 millones de dólares), que contempla una reasignación de recursos entre diferentes sectores, un recorte en rubros relacionados con el acuerdo de paz y un incremento de los recursos destinados al pago del servicio de la deuda. La cifra supera los 555,8 billones de pesos del presupuesto vigente para 2026. El presupuesto del próximo año prevé un déficit fiscal de 9,4% del Producto Interno Bruto (PIB). El Senado aprobó la ley de presupuesto el lunes en la noche con 57 votos a favor y uno en contra, mientras que la Cámara de Representantes lo hizo el martes en la madrugada con 112 votos a favor y uno en contra. "Gracias a todos ustedes por habernos dado este voto de confianza, vamos a lograr sacar al país de esta situación económica tan compleja y para eso el presupuesto, sin lugar a dudas, es un primer paso muy importante", dijo el ministro de Hacienda, Miguel Gómez, después de la aprobación en el Senado. El Gobierno planea presentar al Congreso la denominada "Ley de Rescate" para recortar el gasto público el próximo año, con lo que el déficit fiscal se ajustaría al 7,2% del PIB, según el Ministerio de Hacienda. El presupuesto de gastos de 2027 asigna 141 billones de pesos (44.672 millones de dólares) para el pago de la deuda, 93 billones de pesos (29.464,7 millones de dólares) para educación, 84,6 billones de pesos (26.803 millones de dólares) para salud y 74,9 billones de pesos (23.730 millones de dólares) para defensa. RECORTES DEL GASTO La reasignación de recursos realizada por el Gobierno del presidente Abelardo De La Espriella provocó un recorte en el presupuesto de funcionamiento de la Jurisdicción Especial para la Paz (JEP) y la Unidad de Búsqueda de Personas dadas por Desaparecidas (UBPD), creadas en virtud del acuerdo de paz de 2016 firmado con la antigua guerrilla de las Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionarias de Colombia (FARC). El recorte a la JEP fue de alrededor de 181.000 millones de pesos, recursos que se trasladaron al Ministerio de Defensa, según el Ministerio de Hacienda. La reducción equivale al 23% del presupuesto del tribunal, un recorte mayor que el previsto. El tribunal advirtió que la decisión limitará las investigaciones y los juicios por violaciones de los derechos humanos, dificultará la prestación de asistencia jurídica y apoyo psicológico a las víctimas, así como el pago de sus gastos de viaje, y pondrá en riesgo los planes de seguridad para proteger a las víctimas y a los excombatientes. El presupuesto operativo de la UBPD se redujo en casi un 22%. La unidad, que busca al menos a 137.000 personas desaparecidas durante el conflicto armado, que continúa y ha dejado más de 450.000 muertos, ha advertido que un recorte de esa magnitud pondrá en peligro la toma de muestras de ADN de las familias y unas 10.000 exhumaciones previstas. La cuarta economía de América Latina enfrenta grandes desafíos para poner en orden sus cuentas fiscales, lo que elevará su endeudamiento público este año y el próximo, y la alejará cada vez más de la posibilidad de recuperar el grado de inversión que perdió en 2021. Además, el país sudamericano busca un acuerdo con el Fondo Monetario Internacional para conseguir financiamiento más barato y enfrentar el complicado panorama económico. (1 dólar = 3.156,32 pesos)

item.title: EssilorLuxottica's smart glasses boom runs into tougher regulatory scrutiny
item.description: Smart glasses that resemble ordinary eyewear are under increased scrutiny from European regulators and advocacy groups, leaving investors questioning whether sales can keep booming as Ray-Ban maker EssilorLuxottica reports third-quarter results.
item.dc:creator: Elisa Anzolin, Gianluca Lo Nostro, Elizabeth Howcroft
item.content:encoded: Smart glasses that resemble ordinary eyewear are under increased scrutiny from European regulators and advocacy groups, leaving investors questioning whether sales can keep booming as Ray-Ban maker EssilorLuxottica (ESLX.PA) reports third-quarter results. EssilorLuxottica launched its Ray-Ban Meta (META.O) smart glasses, capable of filming and recording, in 2023 and the market has grown rapidly. Global shipments of AI-enabled glasses jumped to 8.4 million units in 2025 from around 2.1 million in 2024, according to research group Omdia. EssilorLuxottica's Meta eyewear accounted for 81.3% of global shipments in the first half of this year. When it releases its third-quarter results on Tuesday, EssilorLuxottica is not expected to give precise data on the value of smart glasses sales, but may provide an indication. In its second-quarter trading update, it said smart glasses sales [USN:L1N43U0WL TEXT:"nearly doubled"] compared to the same period a year earlier. SOME GOVERNMENTS CONSIDER BANS The resemblance to ordinary eyewear has been a factor in the success of EssilorLuxottica's Meta smart glasses, and is in contrast to Google Glass (GOOGL.O) more than a decade ago, whose bulky, futuristic design limited mainstream consumer appeal. But the design's discretion is troubling to regulators. Last week, the European Data Protection Board, or EDPB, which brings together national privacy regulators, said the devices facilitated covert recording, including of bystanders' conversations. Louis Larere, portfolio manager at French asset manager BDL, echoed that concern. "The fact that smart glasses include a camera, allow users to livestream and instantly share content on social media could become a problem," he said. So far [USN:L6N45R0AS TEXT:"Norway"] has taken the toughest stance among governments, saying earlier this month it planned a temporary ban on the use of AI glasses in selected locations. [USN:L1N45908Z TEXT:"Australia"] said in September it was considering barring the use of camera-equipped smart glasses in government workplaces. In a preliminary, non-binding statement, the EDPB urged manufacturers to combine measures such as visible recording lights, sound alerts and notifications to nearby devices while recording. The authority also suggested limiting live streaming, automatically blurring bystanders' faces and using location-based technical restrictions in sensitive settings like hospitals or schools. PRIVACY CONCERNS MAY LIMIT ADOPTION Ross Gerber, CEO of California-based wealth management firm Gerber Kawasaki, which holds Meta shares, said privacy concerns and social stigma could limit wider adoption even though smart glasses still hold long-term potential. "People will make you feel uncomfortable if you wear them, and people feel uncomfortable wearing them because of this," he said, adding that his pair of Meta glasses was sitting unused in his garage. A Meta spokesperson said the glasses remain popular for music, calls and live translations. "They were built to be noticed which is why every pair with a camera has a bright light on the front that flashes when you take a photo or video you can share with others," they added. "It's important that rules protect people's rights while supporting innovation and consistency across technologies," an EssilorLuxottica spokesperson told Reuters, adding that the company is working to help consumers understand how to use the glasses responsibly and respectfully. Data regulators in Italy and Austria both told Reuters that they were investigating incidents involving smart glasses being used by pupils in schools, and [USN:L1N4590OL TEXT:"France's data watchdog"] previously said it had received a small number of complaints. "Authorities should think about banning these devices in public spaces in a more coordinated manner," Kleanthi Sardeli, a lawyer at European digital rights advocacy group NOYB, told Reuters. Growing privacy concerns could pose a challenge for EssilorLuxottica and Meta as they seek to position AI glasses, which can be used for making calls and listening to music, as a potential future alternative to smartphones. "(Privacy concerns) are a risk to this category. We already saw something similar more than a decade ago with Google Glasses," Cedric Rossi, luxury and consumer goods equity research analyst at Stifel, said. Rossi said Meta's unveiling in September of camera-free [USN:L1N45F121 TEXT:"audio glasses"] was a first step toward addressing regulatory and privacy concerns. However, he added that, without a camera, users cannot fully benefit from the AI capabilities the devices are designed to offer. Other companies, meanwhile, are still drawn to [USN:L4N42O1PB TEXT:"the category"] and Google, in partnership with Samsung (005930.KS) , plans to release its Gemini AI glasses before the end of this year. Apple (AAPL.O) is also expected to release its own smart glasses. BofA analysts in a report this month assessed the regulatory risk as limited and that an outright ban was unlikely even if additional restrictions emerge, particularly in Europe.

item.title: Ataque con drones en zona en disputa entre Sudán y Sudán del Sur deja 150 muertos: funcionario
item.description: El ejército de Sudán llevó a cabo ataques con drones en un mercado en la disputada región de Abyei, causando la muerte de más de 150 personas, afirmaron las autoridades de Sudán del Sur, en otro episodio en una de las semanas más sangrientas de una guerra que se ha extendido más allá de las fronteras de Sudán.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El ejército de Sudán llevó a cabo ataques con drones en un mercado en la disputada región de Abyei, causando la muerte de más de 150 personas, afirmaron las autoridades de Sudán del Sur, en otro episodio en una de las semanas más sangrientas de una guerra que se ha extendido más allá de las fronteras de Sudán. El ataque elevó el número de víctimas mortales de los últimos días a más de 250, lo que pone de relieve la letalidad de los ataques aéreos en la guerra de Sudán, que estalló en abril de 2023 entre las Fuerzas Armadas sudanesas y las Fuerzas de Apoyo Rápido (RSF), de carácter paramilitar. Esto desencadenó una grave crisis humanitaria y atrajo la participación de milicias locales y potencias extranjeras. Yohana Akol Ngor, ministro interino de Información de Abyei, declaró el martes a Reuters que el número de muertos por el ataque al mercado de Abyei del lunes había pasado de 73 a 153, pero que probablemente seguiría aumentando. "El fuego sigue ardiendo. Por lo tanto, el proceso de recuperación de los fallecidos aún continúa. La situación es terrible", afirmó Ngor, añadiendo que algunos cadáveres habían quedado reducidos a cenizas. Un video grabado el martes en el lugar de los hechos y verificado por Reuters mostraba restos carbonizados y retorcidos de vehículos y edificios. Las llamas seguían saliendo de uno de los edificios mientras los residentes inspeccionaban los daños. El funcionario afirmó que el ejército de Sudán era responsable del ataque, sin aportar pruebas. Un portavoz de las fuerzas armadas de Sudán no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. Tres fuentes diplomáticas, un trabajador humanitario y un experto en el conflicto declararon a Reuters que el ataque había alcanzado un depósito de combustible situado en el mercado. Las fuentes diplomáticas indicaron que el depósito había sido utilizado en el pasado por las RSF para abastecer a sus fuerzas. Un portavoz de las RSF no respondió de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios. Abyei es una zona rica en petróleo que está bajo administración conjunta de Sudán del Sur y Sudán, países que reclaman su soberanía. La región sufre frecuentes episodios de violencia, con enfrentamientos en los que suelen participar grupos étnicos rivales o milicias armadas. Funcionarios del Gobierno sudanés, liderado por militares, declararon a Reuters que la RSF opera en algunas zonas de Abyei. Ngor negó la presencia de la RSF en Abyei. Reuters no pudo verificar de inmediato estas afirmaciones. El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de Sudán del Sur dijo en un comunicado emitido a última hora del lunes que los drones atacaron un mercado situado al norte de la localidad de Abyei, pero no especificó el número de víctimas civiles causadas por el ataque. El ministerio dijo que había convocado al embajador sudanés para transmitirle la "enérgica protesta y profunda preocupación del Gobierno respecto al ataque y sus implicaciones para la seguridad de la población civil y la estabilidad de la zona de Abyei".

item.title: Gulf Keystone, ShaMaran agree $601 million oil merger
item.description: Gulf Keystone Petroleum said on Tuesday it would merge with Norway's ShaMaran Petroleum in a $601 million all-share 50-50 deal, creating one of the largest producers in Iraq's oil-rich Kurdistan region.

item.content:encoded: Gulf Keystone Petroleum (GKP.L) said on Tuesday it would merge with Norway's ShaMaran Petroleum (SNMS.OL) in a $601 million all-share 50-50 deal, creating one of the largest producers in Iraq's oil-rich Kurdistan region. Here are some details from the statement: ShaMaran shareholders to receive 0.07533958 Gulf Keystone share for each ShaMaran share held, with Gulf Keystone shareholders to receive a $50 million special dividend Merger combines operations across four Iraqi fields: Shaikan, Atrush, Sarsang and Hamrin Combined company expected to hold 323 million barrels of proved and probable reserves With pro-forma working interest production of 53,000 bpd, combined company ranks among the top 10 European listed independent oil producers Combined group has potential to reach 100,000 barrels of oil per day through development of Shaikan and Hamrin fields, a Gulf Keystone spokesperson said Dealmaking among Middle East-focused oil companies is supported by higher oil prices, with Genel Energy (GENL.L) competing with Norway's DNO (DNO.OL) to buy [USN:L6N45H0B2 TEXT:"Capricorn Energy"] (CNE.L)

item.title: Stocks mostly rise as oil, US yields ease; French stocks fall
item.description: US stock indexes ended mostly higher as oil prices and Treasury yields eased on Tuesday, while French stocks fell as worries about unrest in the country remained.
item.dc:creator: Caroline Valetkevitch, Shashwat Chauhan
item.content:encoded: US stock indexes ended mostly higher as oil prices and Treasury yields eased on Tuesday, while French stocks fell as worries about unrest in the country remained. Helping the blue-chip Dow, 3M (MMM.N) shares shot up 5.8% after it said it was expanding its data-center partnership with Amazon (AMZN.O) . Shares of the industrial conglomerate were also boosted by the company raising its full-year profit forecast. After the closing bell, shares of [USN:L4N4661M0 TEXT:"SpaceX"] (SPCX.O) rose after the company said its third-quarter revenue more than doubled, beating estimates as AI and Starlink grew. The stock fell 0.1% in the regular session. At the same time, [USN:L6N465197 TEXT:"Netflix "] (NFLX.O) fell in after-hours trading as it gave a disappointing quarterly forecast. The stock was down 1.7% in the regular session. Quarterly results from AI heavyweight Meta (META.O) are scheduled for Wednesday. Investors are looking to corporate earnings for evidence that consumers and the broader economy remain resilient, but also that massive AI spending is paying off. "Investors really are waiting for the growth companies to report. Analysts have raised their estimates ... It's going to be by how much do they jump over that elevator bar," said Bruce Zaro, managing director at Granite Wealth Management in Plymouth, Massachusetts. Reflecting some of this nervousness was a 32% drop in South Korean AI [USN:L1N46600F TEXT:"infrastructure company"] Elice Group (0158S0.KQ) , when the stock fell below its initial public offering price in its market debut. Investors are also still assessing the risk that higher interest rates pose to AI stocks. Longer-dated US Treasury yields dropped, with the yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note down 1.5 basis points at 5.121% after falling as low as 5.073% on the day. Yields have risen recently amid worries about inflation. Expectations for a rate hike of at least 25 basis points from the Federal Reserve at its policy meeting next week stand at 17.2%, according to CME FedWatch, down from 22.1% a week ago and 57.6% a month earlier. "This is a market relieved that rates have come down, relieved that there's less volatility in oil prices, even though they remain elevated," said Jake Dollarhide, CEO of Longbow Asset Management in Tulsa, Oklahoma. "Earnings season can distract this market. Earnings season can give this market reason to go higher," he said. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 529.85 points, or 1.02%, to 52,495.88, the S&P 500 (.SPX) rose 21.84 points, or 0.28%, to 7,712.57 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) fell 6.07 points, or 0.02%, to 26,424.82. MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe (.MIWD00000PUS) rose 0.42 points, or 0.04%, to 1,130.40. FRENCH STOCKS FALL, OIL EASES France's cities were [USN:L6N4660DJ TEXT:"calm overnight"] under curfews imposed after last weekend's unrest, while protest groups announced a new round of demonstrations next Saturday. French stocks (.FCHI) fell 0.38%, while the pan-European STOXX 600 (.STOXX) index was down 0.14%. European semiconductor companies including ASML (ASML.AS) and ASMI (ASMI.AS) also were lower. France's government [USN:L6N4660NP TEXT:"bond yields"] climbed further, with investors remaining cautious ahead of the plans for further protests. The unrest in France has underscored the difficulties the French government faces in reducing its large deficit. France's 10-year OAT yield earlier was up 3 basis points at 4.96%; it reached 4.9937%, its highest since July 2002, in early October. The yield gap between OATs and Bunds widened by 5.5 bps to 152.50 bps. The euro was up 0.22% at $1.1235, though traders remained cautious because of the unrest in France. Meanwhile, the [USN:L1N4660RH TEXT:"US dollar weakened"]. The dollar index , which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, fell 0.25% to 101.71. Investors assessed the durability of strong capital inflows into US AI companies. Those inflows have supported the dollar. Higher interest rates, driven partly by growth and inflation expectations tied to the sector, have helped. Oil prices [USN:L1N46601X TEXT:"slipped"] after touching a five-month high. Investors [USN:L1N46601X TEXT:"assessed"] a meeting between the Iranian president and Pakistan's army chief, a key US-Iran mediator, against continued Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure that could disrupt supply. Brent crude futures fell 76 cents, or 0.69%, to settle at $108.79. Earlier in the session, the front-month contract reached $111.99, a five-month high. The November contract for US West Texas Intermediate crude , which expired on Tuesday, settled down $1.87, or 1.8%, at $101.79.

item.title: Trump warns Kansans that US will 'burn' like France if Democrats win
item.description: Trump used violent unrest in France as an argument against Democrats.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, Steve Holland
item.content:encoded:
US President Donald Trump on Monday used [USN:L6N4650BY TEXT:"violent unrest in France"] as an argument against Democrats in his battle to defend a Kansas Senate seat long held by Republicans but in danger of falling to his political opponents. Trump's rally on behalf of Republican incumbent Roger Marshall was his latest foray into conservative states where Republican candidates are on defense due to voter frustrations over the Iran war and rising prices.

"I love you Kansas, but I'm here for a guy named Roger Marshall," Trump said. In a new addition to his stump speech, Trump pointed to widespread protests in France as a scenario that could erupt in the United States unless Republicans win. He provided no evidence. France in recent days has seen some of the worst unrest in years as huge protests over the cost of living and underfunded public services descended into riots and looting. Trump himself has struggled to make goods and services more affordable in the United States. In his speech, Trump turned to anti-immigrant and anti-Muslim rhetoric, the type that he used to fuel his three presidential campaigns. "We're not going to let that happen to this country," he said. "When you see burning steeples and raging fires in France, just remember that is what the radical Dumocrats want to do to America." Trump has been mocking Democrats by calling them Dumocrats. Rights advocates have [USN:L1N4620ZA TEXT:"repeatedly criticized"] Trump for his rhetoric over the years in which he has targeted and mocked immigrants and ethnic minority groups. Civil rights groups say such rhetoric normalizes discriminatory attitudes towards those communities. KANSAS COMPETITION Kansas, a conservative Midwestern state Trump won by 16 points in 2024, has not elected a Democrat to the US Senate in 94 years. First-term Senator Marshall is in a close fight with Democratic candidate Adam Hamilton, pastor of a Methodist megachurch, who is running against Trump’s tariff agenda and what he calls the president's “erratic leadership.” “He wants you to repent for being born White,” Trump said of Hamilton. Marshall, in remarks to the rally, led his campaign argument on cultural issues like stopping "radical Islam." He called Hamilton "too woke" for Kansas because he supports gay pride parades, which the crowd loudly booed. "We need someone who can sort heifers and steers," he said. In response, Hamilton's campaign spokesperson called Marshall's campaign "sinking." "Nothing said at the rally can distract from the fact Kansans are being crushed by rising gas and diesel prices, struggling to access affordable healthcare, and are tired of Washington corruption," the spokesperson, Tyson Brody, said. In a Monday video, Hamilton welcomed Trump to the state and said his supporters have “a place” in his campaign. Hamilton said he will work with Trump when it makes sense and stand up for Kansans when Washington policies hurt farmers and rural hospitals. The tightness of the race is emblematic of the challenges looming for Republicans in the November 3 midterm elections as they try to defy political headwinds and retain control of the Senate and the House of Representatives. Trump is deep into a 32-day campaign blitz, frequently going to friendly areas that he won handily in previous elections. One Republican familiar with Trump's midterm strategy said the president’s attention on rural parts of the country is in response to internal polling showing soft support from men 55 years and younger in rural areas nationwide, a voting bloc crucial to Trump’s 2024 presidential win. ECONOMIC CONCERNS The [USN:L6N46517O TEXT:"latest Reuters/Ipsos poll"], published on Monday, found that 31% of Americans approve of Trump's performance in office, a record low for the president. Democrats need a net gain of four seats in both the US House of Representatives and US Senate to overturn Republicans' narrow 218-214 and 53-47 majorities. In Park City, near Wichita, many rallygoers walked more than a mile across Interstate 135 to reach the rural arena, as a red-and-green truck stop sign flashed its latest prices above their heads: $3.98 for gas and $5.78 for diesel. That is up about 45% compared to average gas prices in the state last year, according to motoring club AAA. Economic concerns were palpable among Trump's most loyal supporters. “Being on disability, I don’t have much, but it seems like the prices are still going up and they need to come down. It feels like you’re having to search or hunt for food," said Monique Mullen, 59, a Republican voter from Hutchinson, Kansas, who takes care of her father. A small bloc of protesters gathered near the arena, including James Nightingale, a self-described independent from Halstead, Kansas. “I’m a farmer from Kansas and the Trump administration has decimated the farm economy in my area. Not only have his tariffs decimated our markets for grain sales, now he is bringing in imported beef from outside the country. What happened to ‘America First’?” he said. Kansans have proven a willingness to cross parties, as voters have elected a Democratic governor, Laura Kelly, for the last two terms. "I don't think it's ever easy to get elected here," said Gina Seman, a Trump voter from Towanda, Kansas, noting that Republican candidates in the past have taken their popularity for granted.

item.title: Trump promises billions in payments to voters ahead of midterm elections
item.description: US President Donald Trump is promising billions of dollars in direct payments to millions of Americans just weeks before the November 3 elections that will determine whether his Republicans will maintain control of the US Congress.
item.dc:creator: Andy Sullivan
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump is promising billions of dollars in direct payments to millions of Americans just weeks before the November 3 elections that will determine whether his Republicans will maintain control of the US Congress. Here is a list of Trump's recent promised giveaways: $8 BILLION TO FARMERS Trump said at a campaign rally in Kansas on October 19 that farmers will get [USN:SPN4650BH TEXT:"$8 billion in one-time payments"] to offset high diesel fuel prices during the fall harvest season. The US Agriculture Department said it would use a formula to cover a portion of "modeled losses" this year. Diesel is widely used in agriculture and trucking, and prices have risen 38% since Trump launched the US war with Iran in February. Democratic Senate candidates in Republican-leaning farm states like Kansas and Iowa have [USN:L6N45Z1B9 TEXT:"harnessed voter discontent"] over high fuel prices to mount competitive races this year. $90 CHECKS TO SENIORS Trump said on October 2 the government will send a [USN:FWN45O0AV TEXT:"$90 payment"] to 20.8 million people enrolled in Medicare Part B, the medical-insurance portion of the government's health plan for seniors. The White House said the one-time payments will help to offset rising healthcare costs. The money will be drawn from a $2 billion fund meant to improve the program. Most of the 70.6 million Americans enrolled in Medicare will not get these checks. Low-income people whose Part B premiums are covered by the program, high-income people who pay an extra fee, and those enrolled in privately run Medicare Advantage programs will not qualify. The standard Part B premium is $202.90 per month. This will be at least the second benefit Trump has targeted at seniors, a politically influential group who vote at high levels in [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"]. Trump's sweeping One Big Beautiful Bill Act enacted last year included a tax break for people over 65, fulfilling a promise he made during the 2024 presidential campaign. $500 CHECKS TO SOME OBAMACARE USERS The administration has also sent payments of $500 to 950,000 people who buy health insurance from the government-run healthcare.gov portal. Many of these people have seen their premiums rise sharply after the Republican-controlled Congress allowed a subsidy package to expire at the end of 2025. The White House says the payments are a refund for what it describes as excessive fees set under former Democratic President Joe Biden. Like the Medicare payments, these checks will not go to all 19 million people who rely on Obamacare — people who get subsidized coverage and people in the 20 states that run their own marketplaces do not qualify. Some 71% of those who qualify live in states that are holding competitive elections for US Senate or governor, according to a [USN:L6N45K16K TEXT:"Reuters analysis"] of government data. $25 MILLION FOR FRAUD TIPSTERS Trump announced a whistleblower program on October 20 that would give awards of up to $30,000 to people who report fraud in government programs. The Justice Department said the program would cost $25 million in total. $5,000 PAYMENTS FOR ALL ADULTS On September 9, Trump promised a [USN:L6N45211D TEXT:"payment of $5,000"] to all US adult citizens, which would cost $1.2 trillion — equal to roughly 16% of the federal budget — if his Republicans held onto Congress in November. However, that idea has gotten little traction in Congress, which would have to sign off on it. PIPELINES AND POWER LINES IN ALASKA The Trump administration announced $150 million in new funding for [USN:L6N45R015 TEXT:"power lines"] in Alaska on October 5, the same day that Vice President JD Vance campaigned in the state for Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, who is facing a tight reelection campaign. The week before, Trump announced plans for a liquefied natural gas pipeline in the state as well, but Vance said details still need to be worked out.
